# axi-core — Specification
> Draft · June 2026

---

## Overview

`axi-core` is a Rust crate of pure agentic response primitives — the
conventions that make tools ergonomic for LLMs regardless of protocol or
language. It is general-purpose: useful to anyone building AXI-compliant
tools, not tied to any specific stack.

It encodes six of the ten [AXI principles](https://axi.md) as typed, tested
Rust: TOON list rendering, key-value single-item rendering, contextual
disclosure (`help[]`), content truncation, definitive empty states, structured
errors with exit codes, idempotency signals, retry delay primitives, and
content-first status responses.

The crate has no protocol knowledge (no MCP, no HTTP, no CLI framework) and
no async runtime dependency. It is pure computation: data in, strings and types
out. TypeScript consumers reach it via the NAPI npm wrapper `axi-core`. Rust
consumers take a direct crates.io or git dep.

---

## Motivation

AXI's 10 design principles describe how to build agent-ergonomic interfaces,
but the principles themselves are implemented ad-hoc — scattered as TypeScript
conventions in MCP servers, implicit CLI output patterns, and per-tool string
formatting. When `axi-core` exists:

- The TOON format has a canonical, tested Rust implementation shared by both
  MCP and CLI consumers
- `help[]` hint construction, `totalCount` formatting, truncation signals, and
  recovery hint shapes are defined once and cannot drift between consumers
- Any agent-facing Rust CLI can import the same primitives directly
- Any TypeScript MCP server or CLI can reach them via the NAPI npm package

A non-agentic tool (infrastructure CLIs, build scripts) uses its own output
conventions and never encounters axi-core. The package boundary enforces the
separation — agentic concepts do not leak into infrastructure.

---

## Non-goals

- **Display-format Markdown** — research-grounded LLM display formatters
  (fields, sections, tables) are the caller's concern. axi-core is the
  `audience: ["assistant"]` compact surface; display rendering for the
  `audience: ["user"]` surface stays in your MCP SDK or application layer.
- **MCP protocol knowledge** — no `content[]`, no `outputSchema`, no
  `structuredContent`. Those are assembled by the calling MCP framework.
- **CLI framework** — no argument parsing, no stdin/stdout handling. That
  belongs to the caller's CLI framework of choice.
- **HTTP client** — no auth handling, no request construction. axi-core
  provides retry delay primitives that a caller plugs into their own HTTP
  client.
- **Async runtime** — zero tokio, zero async-std. All functions are sync
  and pure. Callers own retry loops and timeout semantics.
- **Full retry implementation** — axi-core provides `RetryConfig`,
  `parse_retry_after()`, and `next_retry_delay()`. The actual retry loop
  (sleep + re-execute) stays in the caller.
- **Caching** — callers should use `moka` or equivalent. axi-core does not
  include a cache.
- **Logging / telemetry** — Rust consumers use the `tracing` crate
  independently.
- **Schema validation** — input validation is the caller's concern.
- **MCP server bootstrapping** — `server.tool()`, tool discovery, deferred
  loading. Protocol-specific, stays in your MCP SDK.

---

## Consumer map

```
Any Rust CLI binary
  Cargo.toml dep on axi-core (crates.io or git)
  Render --format toon via axi_core::render_toon()
  Full access to all modules — no NAPI overhead

Any TypeScript CLI
  npm dep on axi-core
  --format toon dispatch calls into NAPI wrapper
  Same output; NAPI boundary is transparent

Any TypeScript MCP server
  npm dep on axi-core
  Renders TOON for audience:["assistant"] content block
  Assembles MCP content[] from the returned string
```

---

## TOON format specification

TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) is the agent-facing list format.
It front-loads structure (type, count, field names) so the LLM has full
context before reading any row, then encodes rows as compact comma-separated
values. Field names appear once in the header rather than once per row.

**Why TOON for lists?**
Standard JSON repeats field names on every item. Markdown key-value format
repeats field names per item, which is ideal for single items and small sets
but expensive at scale. TOON trades per-item field repetition for a one-time
header, saving proportionally more tokens as N grows. For lists of 5+ items,
TOON is the better token budget choice. For single items or small metadata
blocks, key-value format remains preferred — see `kv::render_kv()`.

AXI's benchmark shows this class of output optimization delivers approximately
40% token reduction over equivalent JSON for list data.

### Grammar

```
document     ::= type_header NEWLINE row+ totalcount? help_block?
type_header  ::= type_name "[" count "]" "{" field_list "}" ":"
type_name    ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*                 (snake_case)
count        ::= [0-9]+                            (items in this response)
field_list   ::= field_name ("," field_name)*
field_name   ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*
row          ::= "  " value ("," value)* NEWLINE   (2-space indent)
value        ::= scalar | quoted
scalar       ::= [^,\n"]*
quoted       ::= '"' ( [^"\\] | "\\" . )* '"'     (for values with commas)
totalcount   ::= "totalCount: " [0-9]+ NEWLINE     (total available, may exceed count)
help_block   ::= "help[" [0-9]+ "]:" NEWLINE hint+
hint         ::= "  " [^\n]+ NEWLINE
```

### Examples

**List response:**
```
issues[3]{number,title,state}:
  42,Fix login redirect,open
  43,Add dark mode,open
  44,"Update deps, bump major",closed
totalCount: 47
help[2]:
  Call get_issue with number=<number> for full detail
  Call list_issues with state=open to filter
```

**Truncated field value:**
```
components[2]{name,description,tokens}:
  Button,"Primary action element (148 chars truncated — use full=true)",12
  Icon,"Scalable vector icon (203 chars truncated — use full=true)",8
totalCount: 84
help[1]:
  Call get_component with name=<name> and full=true for complete description
```

**Empty state:**
```
issues[0]{}:
totalCount: 0
help[1]:
  Try list_issues with a broader filter
```

**Single recovery hint (no list):**
```
help[1]:
  Retry create_item with suggestedParams: { project: "PROJ", type: "Task" }
```

### Escaping rules

- Values containing commas MUST be quoted
- Values containing double-quote characters use backslash escape: `\"`
- Values containing newlines MUST be truncated before rendering — TOON
  does not support multi-line cell values
- Null/absent values render as empty scalar: `val1,,val3`
- Boolean values: `true` / `false` literals
- Numeric values: rendered without quotes

---

## Rust public API

### Crate root (`src/lib.rs`)

```rust
pub mod toon;
pub mod kv;
pub mod hints;
pub mod truncate;
pub mod empty;
pub mod error;
pub mod idempotency;
pub mod resilience;
pub mod status;
pub mod response;
pub mod recovery;

// Top-level re-exports for the common path
pub use hints::Hint;
pub use response::{AgentResponse, OutputFormat};
pub use toon::render_toon;
pub use kv::render_kv;
pub use error::{AxiError, ErrorCode};
pub use idempotency::{already_done, PartialSuccess, FailedOp};
pub use resilience::{RetryConfig, parse_retry_after, next_retry_delay};
pub use status::StatusResponse;
pub use truncate::{truncate, truncate_inline};
pub use empty::empty_state;
pub use recovery::RecoveryHint;
```

---

### `toon` — list rendering for N uniform-schema items

TOON is the agent-facing format for lists. It front-loads structure (type,
count, field names) and encodes rows as compact comma-separated values.
Field names appear once in the header rather than once per row. Preferred
over key-value format for lists of 5+ items where token savings compound;
for single items, use `kv::render_kv()` instead.

```rust
pub struct ToonOptions {
    /// Max cell value length before inline truncation.
    /// Appends "(N chars truncated — use full=true)" when exceeded.
    /// Default: 200
    pub max_cell_len: usize,
    /// Total items available. May exceed rows rendered.
    /// Emitted as "totalCount: N" line when Some.
    pub total_count: Option<u64>,
}

impl Default for ToonOptions { ... }

/// Render items as TOON.
/// Panics in debug if any row.len() != fields.len().
/// Returns empty-state TOON when items is empty.
pub fn render_toon(
    type_name: &str,
    items: &[Vec<Value>],
    fields: &[&str],
    hints: &[Hint],
    opts: ToonOptions,
) -> String

pub enum Value {
    Str(String),
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
    Bool(bool),
    Null,
}

impl From<&str>           for Value { ... }
impl From<String>         for Value { ... }
impl From<i64>            for Value { ... }
impl From<bool>           for Value { ... }
impl From<Option<String>> for Value { ... }
```

---

### `kv` — single-item key-value rendering

Markdown key-value format for single items and small mixed-type metadata
sets. Benchmarks of LLM format retrieval accuracy show this format performs
strongly for single-item or small-N data where field name repetition is
acceptable. Column width is determined by the longest key.

```rust
pub struct KvItem {
    pub key:   String,
    pub value: KvValue,
}

pub enum KvValue {
    Text(String),
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64, u8),    // value, decimal places
    Bool(bool),
    Duration(std::time::Duration),
    Missing,           // renders as "—"
}

/// Render key-value pairs with aligned columns.
/// Appends totalCount and help[] block when provided.
pub fn render_kv(
    items: &[KvItem],
    total_count: Option<u64>,
    hints: &[Hint],
) -> String
```

Output for a single item:
```
name:         Button
variant:      primary
tokens:       12
description:  Primary action element
totalCount: 1
help[1]:
  Call list_components to see related
```

---

### `hints` — contextual disclosure blocks

```rust
pub struct Hint(pub String);

impl Hint {
    pub fn new(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self
}

/// Render a standalone help[] block.
/// Returns empty string when hints is empty.
pub fn render_hints(hints: &[Hint]) -> String

/// Append a help[] block to an existing body string.
/// Returns body unchanged when hints is empty.
pub fn append_hints(body: &str, hints: &[Hint]) -> String
```

---

### `truncate` — size-bounded output with escape hatches

```rust
pub struct Truncated {
    pub content:      String,
    pub truncated:    bool,
    pub original_len: usize,
    /// "(N chars truncated — use full=true)" — None when not truncated
    pub signal:       Option<String>,
}

/// Truncate content to at most `limit` chars.
pub fn truncate(content: &str, limit: usize) -> Truncated

/// Truncate and append the signal inline.
/// Returns original string when it fits within limit.
pub fn truncate_inline(content: &str, limit: usize) -> String
```

---

### `empty` — definitive zero states

```rust
/// Render an explicit empty-state TOON response.
/// Callers MUST use this — never return silent empty output.
///
/// Produces:
///   type_name[0]{}:
///   totalCount: 0
pub fn empty_state(type_name: &str) -> String

/// Empty state with contextual hints.
pub fn empty_state_with_hints(type_name: &str, hints: &[Hint]) -> String
```

---

### `error` — structured errors with exit codes

AXI P6: errors go to stdout (not stderr), carry exit codes, carry hints,
and never block on interactive prompts. `AxiError` encodes this as a type.

The HTTP status → ErrorCode mapping is NOT in axi-core — callers produce
an `ErrorCode` after interpreting whatever failure occurred. This keeps the
module free of HTTP knowledge.

```rust
pub struct AxiError {
    pub code:        ErrorCode,
    pub message:     String,
    pub hints:       Vec<Hint>,
    pub recovery:    Option<RecoveryHint>,
    pub retryable:   bool,
    pub retry_after: Option<std::time::Duration>,
}

pub enum ErrorCode {
    // Non-retryable — agent should not retry without changing params
    InvalidInput,    // bad parameters
    NotFound,        // resource absent
    Unauthorized,    // auth failure
    Forbidden,       // permission denied
    Conflict,        // resource state mismatch

    // Retryable — agent may retry same call
    RateLimited,     // 429 — check retry_after
    Unavailable,     // 503
    Timeout,         // request timed out
    ExternalFailure, // downstream error
}

impl AxiError {
    pub fn new(code: ErrorCode, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self
    pub fn hint(mut self, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self
    pub fn recovery(mut self, r: RecoveryHint) -> Self
    pub fn retry_after(mut self, d: std::time::Duration) -> Self

    /// Render to stdout-ready string with hints attached.
    pub fn render(&self) -> String

    /// AXI exit codes: 0 = success/already_done, 1 = all other errors.
    /// Callers should not invent additional codes.
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32
}
```

---

### `idempotency` — already-done signals and partial success

Provides types and rendering for idempotency checks, already-done detection,
and partial-success reporting. The caller owns the persistence layer that
tracks what has been done; axi-core provides the rendering contract.

```rust
/// A canonical idempotency key.
pub struct IdempotencyKey(pub String);

impl IdempotencyKey {
    /// Construct from operation name + a stable string representation of inputs.
    pub fn new(operation: &str, stable_input: &str) -> Self
    /// Construct from operation name + raw bytes (SHA-256 hashed).
    pub fn from_hash(operation: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Self
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str
}

/// Render an already-done response.
/// Exits 0 — this is a successful no-op, not an error.
/// Produces a kv block with operation status + hints.
pub fn already_done(
    operation: &str,
    summary: &str,
    hints: &[Hint],
) -> String

/// Partial success: some operations completed, some failed.
pub struct PartialSuccess {
    pub completed: Vec<String>,
    pub failed:    Vec<FailedOp>,
    pub skipped:   Vec<String>,
}

pub struct FailedOp {
    pub operation: String,
    pub reason:    String,
    pub recovery:  Option<RecoveryHint>,
}

impl PartialSuccess {
    pub fn render(&self) -> String
    /// 0 when all operations completed or skipped.
    /// 1 when any operations failed.
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32
}
```

---

### `resilience` — retry delay primitives

Pure computation only — no async, no network, no sleep. Callers build the
actual retry loop; axi-core provides the delay calculation and header
parsing.

```rust
pub struct RetryConfig {
    pub max_attempts:   u32,                    // default: 3
    pub initial_delay:  std::time::Duration,    // default: 1s
    pub max_delay:      std::time::Duration,    // default: 30s
    pub backoff_factor: f64,                    // default: 2.0
    pub jitter:         bool,                   // default: true
}

impl Default for RetryConfig { ... }

/// Parse a Retry-After header value.
/// Accepts integer seconds ("120") or HTTP-date ("Wed, 21 Oct 2025 07:28:00 GMT").
/// Returns None for malformed or absent values.
pub fn parse_retry_after(value: &str) -> Option<std::time::Duration>

/// Compute the next retry delay.
/// Applies exponential backoff, optional jitter, and clamps to max_delay.
/// Respects retry_after when provided — returns the larger of backoff and header.
pub fn next_retry_delay(
    attempt: u32,
    config: &RetryConfig,
    retry_after: Option<std::time::Duration>,
) -> std::time::Duration

/// Whether a status code is conventionally retryable.
/// Returns true for: 429, 502, 503, 504.
pub fn is_retryable_status(status: u16) -> bool
```

Usage pattern for a caller implementing their own retry loop:
```rust
let config = RetryConfig::default();
for attempt in 0..config.max_attempts {
    match call_api() {
        Ok(result) => return Ok(result),
        Err(e) if is_retryable_status(e.status) => {
            let retry_after = e.retry_after_header
                .and_then(|h| parse_retry_after(&h));
            let delay = next_retry_delay(attempt, &config, retry_after);
            sleep(delay).await;
        }
        Err(e) => return Err(e),
    }
}
```

---

### `status` — content-first orientation responses (P8)

P8: bare tool invocation shows live state, not help text. `StatusResponse`
is what any tool returns when called with no arguments.

Built on `kv::render_kv()`. Health signals surface degraded state alongside
nominal metrics — approaching rate limit, stale index, auth expiry.

```rust
pub struct StatusItem {
    pub key:    String,
    pub value:  kv::KvValue,
    pub health: Option<Health>,
}

pub enum Health {
    Ok,
    Degraded(String),   // "(reason)" appended inline
    Error(String),
}

pub struct StatusResponse {
    pub tool_name:   &'static str,
    pub description: &'static str,
    pub items:       Vec<StatusItem>,
    pub hints:       Vec<Hint>,
}

impl StatusResponse {
    pub fn render(&self) -> String
}
```

Example output:
```
tool:         my-search-tool
description:  Semantic code search and symbol analysis
index:        ready
files:        2847
cache:        warm (98MB / 100MB)  [DEGRADED: approaching limit]
last-updated: 4 minutes ago
help[1]:
  Run `search <query>` to search
```

---

### `recovery` — recovery hint shapes

```rust
pub struct RecoveryHint {
    pub tool:   String,
    pub params: Vec<(String, serde_json::Value)>,
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

impl RecoveryHint {
    pub fn new(tool: impl Into<String>) -> Self
    pub fn param(mut self, key: impl Into<String>, val: impl Into<serde_json::Value>) -> Self
    pub fn reason(mut self, reason: impl Into<String>) -> Self
}

/// Render recovery hints as a help[] block with suggestedParams.
pub fn render_recovery(hints: &[RecoveryHint]) -> String
```

---

### `response` — AgentResponse builder

The primary integration point. Composes all modules into a single builder.
Callers use this rather than calling individual render functions directly.

```rust
pub struct AgentResponse {
    type_name:        String,
    items:            Vec<Vec<Value>>,
    fields:           Vec<String>,
    single_item:      Vec<kv::KvItem>,
    total_count:      Option<u64>,
    hints:            Vec<Hint>,
    recovery:         Vec<RecoveryHint>,
    truncate_cells:   usize,
}

pub enum OutputFormat {
    /// TOON — token-efficient list format for audience:["assistant"]
    Toon,
    /// Markdown-KV — for single items and status
    Kv,
    /// Compact JSON — for structuredContent or client tooling
    Json,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    pub fn new(type_name: impl Into<String>) -> Self

    // List path (→ TOON)
    pub fn items(mut self, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>, fields: &[&str]) -> Self
    pub fn total_count(mut self, n: u64) -> Self

    // Single-item path (→ KV)
    pub fn kv_items(mut self, items: Vec<kv::KvItem>) -> Self

    // Shared
    pub fn hint(mut self, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self
    pub fn hints(mut self, hints: Vec<Hint>) -> Self
    pub fn recovery_hint(mut self, r: RecoveryHint) -> Self
    pub fn truncate_cells_at(mut self, limit: usize) -> Self

    pub fn render(&self, format: OutputFormat) -> String
    pub fn render_toon(&self) -> String    // shorthand
    pub fn render_kv(&self) -> String      // shorthand
    pub fn render_json(&self) -> serde_json::Value
    pub fn render_hints_only(&self) -> String
}
```

---

## NAPI npm package — `axi-core`

Follows the standard napi-rs dual-crate pattern:
- Feature-gated `Cargo.toml` with `napi` feature
- `napi-rs` with `napi-derive` macros
- `serde_json::Value` for FFI boundary
- Platform-aware binary loading (`loadBinding`)
- TypeScript fallback export for environments without the native binary
- Cross-compiled via `cargo-zigbuild` for `darwin-arm64` + `linux-x64-musl`

### TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`)

```typescript
export interface ToonOptions {
  /** Max cell value length before truncation. Default: 200 */
  truncateCellsAt?: number;
  /** Total items available. Emitted as totalCount: N when provided. */
  totalCount?: number;
}

/** Scalar cell value. Objects and arrays must be flattened before rendering. */
export type CellValue = string | number | boolean | null;

export interface RenderToonOptions extends ToonOptions {
  typeName: string;
  fields: string[];
  items: CellValue[][];
  hints?: string[];
}

/** Render a list of items as TOON. */
export declare function renderToon(opts: RenderToonOptions): string;

/** Build a standalone help[] block. Returns empty string when hints is empty. */
export declare function renderHints(hints: string[]): string;

/** Append a help[] block to an existing body string. */
export declare function appendHints(body: string, hints: string[]): string;

export interface TruncateResult {
  content: string;
  truncated: boolean;
  originalLen: number;
  /** "(N chars truncated — use full=true)" — undefined when not truncated */
  signal?: string;
}

/** Truncate content to at most limit chars. */
export declare function truncate(content: string, limit: number): TruncateResult;

/** Truncate and append the signal inline. Returns original string when it fits. */
export declare function truncateInline(content: string, limit: number): string;

/** Render a definitive empty-state TOON response. */
export declare function emptyState(typeName: string, hints?: string[]): string;

export interface RecoveryHintParam {
  key: string;
  value: unknown;
}

export interface RecoveryHintInput {
  tool: string;
  params?: RecoveryHintParam[];
  reason?: string;
}

/** Render recovery hints as a help[] block with suggestedParams. */
export declare function renderRecovery(hints: RecoveryHintInput[]): string;

/** High-level builder — mirrors AgentResponse Rust API. */
export declare class AgentResponse {
  constructor(typeName: string);
  items(rows: CellValue[][], fields: string[]): this;
  totalCount(n: number): this;
  hint(hint: string): this;
  hints(hints: string[]): this;
  truncateCellsAt(limit: number): this;
  renderToon(): string;
  renderJson(): unknown;
  renderHintsOnly(): string;
}
```

---

## What this crate provides vs what stays in your application

### Formalising conventions that are typically implicit

| Concept | Where it usually lives | Provided as |
|---|---|---|
| Contextual hints after output | Implicit strings per tool | `hints::Hint`, `render_hints()`, `append_hints()` |
| Total count on list responses | Number passed ad-hoc | `ToonOptions::total_count`, `totalCount:` line |
| Recovery hints on failure | Ad-hoc per server/tool | `recovery::RecoveryHint`, `render_recovery()` |
| Retry delay calculation | Inside caller's retry loop | `resilience::next_retry_delay()` |
| Retry-After header parsing | Ad-hoc string parsing | `resilience::parse_retry_after()` |
| Retryable status classification | Hardcoded booleans per caller | `resilience::is_retryable_status()` |
| Error classification shape | Ad-hoc per tool | `error::AxiError`, `error::ErrorCode` |
| Empty state handling | Ad-hoc per tool (often silent) | `empty::empty_state()` |
| Truncation | Ad-hoc per tool, no standard signal | `truncate::truncate()`, `truncate_inline()` |

### Genuinely new — does not exist as a shared primitive today

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| TOON renderer | New format — token-efficient list encoding for agent context windows |
| `kv::render_kv()` | Single-item Markdown-KV with aligned columns; no standard Rust equivalent |
| `status::StatusResponse` | Typed P8 content-first orientation response — novel primitive |
| `idempotency::already_done()` | Typed already-done signal with canonical output format |
| `idempotency::PartialSuccess` | General partial-success reporting with per-op recovery hints |
| `idempotency::IdempotencyKey` | Canonical key construction with stable hashing |
| `AgentResponse` builder | Unified construction API across all consumers |
| NAPI wrapper | Cross-language bridge — TypeScript authors never write Rust |
| Formal TOON grammar | Canonical spec enabling interoperability and testability |
| `render_hints_only()` | Append hints to an existing body without re-rendering |

### Stays in your application code

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| Display Markdown formatters | Display-surface formatting; `audience: ["user"]` |
| MCP `content[]` assembly | Protocol knowledge |
| `outputSchema` wiring | Tied to your schema validation library |
| Tool annotations | MCP SDK concern |
| MCP server bootstrapping | Protocol-specific |
| HTTP client + auth | Operational concerns with too many deployment shapes |
| LRU cache | General utility, not AXI-specific |
| Full async retry loop | Requires async runtime |
| Structured logging | `tracing` or similar, caller's choice |
| Schema validation | Tied to your type system |

---

## Feature flags

```toml
[features]
default = []
napi = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]
cli  = []     # reserved for terminal-width-aware rendering (colours, wrap)

[dependencies]
serde      = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

[dependencies.napi]
version  = "2"
optional = true

[dependencies.napi-derive]
version  = "2"
optional = true

[build-dependencies.napi-build]
version  = "1"
optional = true
```

No async runtime dependency. No tokio, no async-std. All public functions are
sync. The `cli` feature is reserved for terminal-aware rendering (line wrapping,
colour codes for health signals in `status::StatusResponse`) — out of scope for v1.

---

## Performance contract

| Operation | Target | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `render_toon()` — 100 items, 4 fields | < 500µs | Simple string allocation, no I/O |
| `render_toon()` — 1000 items, 4 fields | < 3ms | Linear in N×fields |
| `render_kv()` — 10 items | < 20µs | Column-width scan + string join |
| `render_hints()` — 5 hints | < 10µs | Trivial string join |
| `truncate_inline()` | < 5µs | Single pass, char boundary safe |
| `parse_retry_after()` | < 2µs | String parse only |
| `next_retry_delay()` | < 1µs | Pure arithmetic |
| NAPI boundary overhead | < 5µs | Established from napi-rs benchmarks |

**Allocation:** `render_toon()` pre-allocates output capacity from
`items.len() × avg_row_estimate`. All functions are allocation-bounded —
no references held across call boundaries.

**Thread safety:** All public functions are stateless pure functions.
`AgentResponse` is `Send + Sync`. NAPI wrapper uses napi-rs safe threading.

Benchmarks via `criterion`. Run in CI on PRs touching `crates/axi-core/src/`.

---

## Testing strategy

### Unit tests (in-crate)
- TOON grammar: one test per grammar production
- KV: alignment, unicode keys, missing values, all KvValue variants
- Escaping: commas, quotes, null, empty string, unicode
- Truncation: exact boundary, under, over, unicode boundary safety
- Hints: empty, single, multiple, long strings
- Empty state: with and without hints
- Recovery: single, multiple, with/without params and reason
- Error: each ErrorCode variant renders + exit codes
- Idempotency: `already_done` format, `PartialSuccess` with mixed results
- Resilience: `parse_retry_after` — integer seconds, HTTP-date, malformed;
  `next_retry_delay` — backoff progression, jitter bounds, Retry-After respect
- Status: all health states, degraded rendering
- `AgentResponse` builder: all method combinations, correct format dispatch

### Property tests (proptest)
- `render_toon()` output is valid per grammar for arbitrary inputs
- `truncate_inline()` never returns string longer than `limit + signal_len`
- TOON round-trip: render → parse (test-only parser) → compare values
- `parse_retry_after()` never panics on arbitrary strings
- `next_retry_delay()` always returns value within `[initial_delay, max_delay]`

### Snapshot tests (insta)
- Canonical TOON examples from this spec
- KV column alignment across different key lengths
- Status response with mixed health signals
- Format stability — prevents accidental format drift

### NAPI integration tests (Jest)
- Each NAPI export with representative inputs
- Error cases: mismatched row lengths, oversized inputs, null values
- `AgentResponse` builder via NAPI, all paths
- Platform binary loading on CI matrix (darwin-arm64, linux-x64-musl)

### Consumer integration tests
- MCP consumer: `audience: ["assistant"]` block is valid TOON
- CLI consumer: `--format toon` output is valid TOON

---

## Crate layout

```
axi-core/
  Cargo.toml
  build.rs                      # napi-build (conditional on napi feature)
  src/
    lib.rs                      # public API, re-exports, crate-level docs
    toon/
      mod.rs                    # render_toon(), ToonOptions, Value
      escape.rs                 # comma/quote/null escaping
      render.rs                 # string assembly with pre-allocated capacity
    kv/
      mod.rs                    # render_kv(), KvItem, KvValue
    hints.rs                    # Hint, render_hints(), append_hints()
    truncate.rs                 # Truncated, truncate(), truncate_inline()
    empty.rs                    # empty_state(), empty_state_with_hints()
    error.rs                    # AxiError, ErrorCode
    idempotency.rs              # IdempotencyKey, already_done(), PartialSuccess
    resilience.rs               # RetryConfig, parse_retry_after(), next_retry_delay()
    status.rs                   # StatusItem, StatusResponse, Health
    recovery.rs                 # RecoveryHint, render_recovery()
    response.rs                 # AgentResponse builder, OutputFormat
    napi.rs                     # #[napi] exports (napi feature only)
  benches/
    toon_render.rs
    kv_render.rs
  tests/
    toon_integration.rs
    kv_integration.rs
    resilience_integration.rs
    idempotency_integration.rs
    snapshot_tests.rs           # insta snapshots

packages/axi-core/              # NAPI wrapper (optional, for npm publish)
  Cargo.toml                    # napi feature, napi-rs build
  package.json                  # axi-core
  index.js                      # loadBinding + TS fallback
  index.d.ts                    # TypeScript types (see NAPI section)
  src/
    lib.rs                      # #[napi] exports wrapping crate functions
  __test__/
    index.test.mjs              # Jest NAPI integration tests
```

---

## Versioning and release

- Published to [crates.io](https://crates.io) as `axi-core`
- npm package published to [npmjs.com](https://npmjs.com) as `axi-core`
- NAPI binary cross-compiled via `cargo-zigbuild`:
  - `darwin-arm64`
  - `linux-x64-musl`

**SemVer contract:**
- **Patch** — bug fixes; TOON output identical or more correct
- **Minor** — new API surface (new module, new method on `AgentResponse`)
- **Major** — TOON format change; any existing rendered output would differ

Format changes are major versions. Consumers should treat the rendered
string as a contract.

---

## Open questions

**Q1 — TOON vs Markdown-KV for agent-facing list responses**
AXI benchmarks the efficiency gains at the CLI/MCP level, but not the
downstream LLM retrieval accuracy of TOON vs Markdown-KV for list data.
Before treating TOON as universally superior for the `audience: ["assistant"]`
surface, run a retrieval accuracy experiment: same list data, TOON vs
Markdown-KV, retrieval task, across a few model sizes. If Markdown-KV wins
on retrieval accuracy despite higher token cost, the right call for MCP
consumers may be to use Markdown-KV even for lists. The crate ships either
way — the question is which format callers should default to.

**Q2 — External Rust consumer strategy**
For external Rust binaries to depend on `axi-core`, options:
(a) crates.io publish — cleanest for public consumers once API is stable
(b) git dep with tag: `axi-core = { git = "...", tag = "v0.x.y" }` — good
    for early adopters before crates.io publish
(c) private cargo registry — overhead not worth it

Recommend (b) during development, (a) at first stable release. Gate
crates.io publish behind at least one real consumer integration test.

**Q3 — `cli` feature scope**
Reserved for terminal-aware rendering. If `--format toon` in a human
terminal context should wrap long rows or colourize the header, the `cli`
feature is where that lives. Out of scope for v1 — axi-core v1 targets
agent consumers only, not human-readable terminal output.

**Q4 — `AgentResponse` builder vs standalone functions**
The spec proposes both: low-level functions (`render_toon()`, `render_hints()`)
and a high-level builder (`AgentResponse`). If the builder is the only
thing NAPI-exported, the low-level functions are Rust-only. If both are
exported, the NAPI surface grows. Recommend: export the builder and
`renderHints()`/`appendHints()` only — low-level functions are implementation
details available to Rust consumers.

**Q5 — Recovery hint format**
The current spec uses `serde_json::Value` for param values — type information
is lost at the boundary. This is acceptable for display (agents read the
rendered string) but may not be acceptable if `structuredContent` in an
MCP context needs to carry typed recovery hints for client programmatic use.
If so, `RecoveryHint` needs a more precise type model. Confirm scope before
implementing.

---

## Supplement — implementation notes and design rationale

### `AgentResponse` format routing

The builder routes to TOON or KV based on which items method the caller uses,
not on item count. The caller is responsible for choosing the right format:

```rust
// List of uniform-schema items → TOON
AgentResponse::new("issues")
    .items(rows, &["number", "title", "state"])   // → render_toon()

// Single item or mixed-type metadata → KV
AgentResponse::new("issue")
    .kv_items(vec![
        KvItem { key: "number".into(), value: KvValue::Int(42) },
        KvItem { key: "title".into(),  value: KvValue::Text("Fix login".into()) },
    ])                                             // → render_kv()
```

**Guidance:** use `.items()` when all rows share the same schema and there
are 5 or more of them — TOON's token savings compound with N. Use
`.kv_items()` for single items, mixed-type status data, or any case where
the field names differ per row. A single-item `.items()` call works but
produces a TOON header with one row, which is less readable and offers no
token advantage over KV.

---

### `IdempotencyKey` — stable input serialisation

`IdempotencyKey::from_hash(operation, data)` hashes the raw bytes of `data`.
For the key to be canonical across calls with the same logical input, `data`
must be produced deterministically:

- **Maps and structs:** sort keys alphabetically before serialising to JSON.
  `serde_json::to_vec` on a `HashMap` produces non-deterministic key order.
  Use `BTreeMap` or a sorted intermediate representation.
- **Floats:** avoid floating-point values in idempotency keys — representation
  varies by architecture. Round to a fixed decimal or convert to integers.
- **Timestamps:** exclude request-time fields (created_at, request_id) unless
  the intent is a per-request key rather than a per-operation key.

```rust
// Correct: BTreeMap serialises with sorted keys
let mut params: BTreeMap<&str, serde_json::Value> = BTreeMap::new();
params.insert("project", json!("PROJ"));
params.insert("type",    json!("Task"));
let key = IdempotencyKey::from_hash("create_item", &serde_json::to_vec(&params)?);

// Incorrect: HashMap key order is non-deterministic
let params: HashMap<&str, _> = /* ... */;
let key = IdempotencyKey::from_hash("create_item", &serde_json::to_vec(&params)?);
// ^ same logical input may produce different keys on different calls
```

---

### `is_retryable_status()` — why 500 is excluded

The default retryable set is `{ 429, 502, 503, 504 }`. HTTP 500 (Internal
Server Error) is intentionally absent.

429 and 50x gateway errors (502, 503, 504) represent transient conditions —
rate limits and upstream unavailability — where the same request is likely
to succeed after a delay. 500 represents a server-side bug. Retrying a 500
without changing anything about the request will produce the same 500. Worse,
retrying write operations that returned 500 may produce duplicate side effects
if the server processed the request before erroring.

Callers that genuinely need to retry 500s (some APIs use it for transient
conditions) can implement their own `is_retryable` predicate and pass it to
their retry loop independently of `is_retryable_status()`.

```rust
// Default: 429, 502, 503, 504 only
if is_retryable_status(status) { ... }

// Custom: caller adds 500 for a specific API known to use it transiently
let retryable = is_retryable_status(status) || status == 500;
```

---

### `render_hints_only()` — the three-surface seam

This method exists to support MCP frameworks that implement a three-surface
response pattern: one content block for agent consumption
(`audience: ["assistant"]`), one for display (`audience: ["user"]`), and a
`structuredContent` payload for client tooling. In this pattern, the display
body is rendered via the framework's own Markdown or rich-text layer, while
the agent-facing block combines TOON output with a `help[]` trailer.

Without `render_hints_only()`, framework code that has already rendered a
display body would need to reconstruct an `AgentResponse` just to get a
formatted `help[]` block to append to the agent surface.

```typescript
// Example: MCP framework TypeScript (simplified)
function assembleToolResult(opts: RespondOpts): ToolResult {
  const userBody      = renderDisplayMarkdown(opts.body);    // display surface → audience:["user"]
  const hintsBlock    = axiCore.renderHintsOnly(opts.hints); // axi-core → append to assistant body
  const assistantBody = opts.assistant                       // caller-provided TOON
      ?? (userBody + "\n" + hintsBlock);                     // fallback: display body + hints

  return {
    content: [
      { type: "text", text: assistantBody,
        annotations: { audience: ["assistant"], priority: 1.0 } },
      { type: "text", text: userBody,
        annotations: { audience: ["user"],      priority: 0.5 } },
    ],
    structuredContent: opts.structured ?? null,
  };
}
```

`render_hints_only()` is the narrow seam between axi-core and the calling
framework's rendering layer — it allows the `help[]` format to be owned by
Rust without requiring the framework to understand TOON.

---

### `parse_retry_after()` — format details

Accepts either of the two forms defined in RFC 7231 §7.1.3:

| Form | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Integer seconds | `"120"` | Seconds to wait from response time |
| HTTP-date | `"Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT"` | Absolute datetime, UTC only |

Returns `None` for any malformed value — including valid HTTP-dates that are
in the past. Callers should treat `None` as "use backoff only" and proceed
with `next_retry_delay()` passing `retry_after: None`.

Does not validate that an HTTP-date is in the future. If a server returns a
past date (clock skew or bug), `parse_retry_after()` will return a zero or
very small duration. `next_retry_delay()` internally clamps: the returned
duration is always at least `config.initial_delay` and at most
`config.max_delay`, regardless of what `parse_retry_after()` returns.

```rust
let retry_after = parse_retry_after(header_value);
let delay = next_retry_delay(attempt, &config, retry_after);
// next_retry_delay() already clamps to initial_delay minimum — no extra handling needed
```

---

### `outputSchema` is in the LLM context

A precision point that matters for token budget planning in MCP servers that
use progressive disclosure or deferred tool loading:

- **`outputSchema`** on a tool definition is part of the `tools/list` response.
  It IS injected into the LLM context window at session start alongside
  `inputSchema`. It adds schema tokens — roughly +15% on the schema component.
  It is a one-time cost that amortises across the session as a prepaid
  reasoning contract.

- **`structuredContent`** in a tool result is client-consumed only. It does
  NOT enter the LLM context window.

This matters for deferred tool loading: adding `outputSchema` to tools that
are not yet loaded would add schema tokens before those tools are called,
defeating the purpose of deferral. `outputSchema` should only be defined on
always-loaded tools, or it should be excluded from `tools/list` for deferred
tools and supplied only when the tool is actually invoked.

If your MCP framework auto-registers `outputSchema` from tool definitions,
ensure it respects the deferred/always-loaded boundary when constructing
`tools/list` responses.

---

### Build-time P4 — pre-computed aggregates at CI time

AXI Principle 4 (pre-computed aggregates) is typically discussed as a runtime
convention: always return `totalCount`, pre-filter before responding, emit
summaries instead of raw data. But the same principle applies at build time,
and that application is more powerful.

**The pattern:** any deterministic computation that a tool needs repeatedly is
a candidate for pre-computation in CI rather than per-request execution at
runtime.

**Canonical example: a build-time component index**

Consider a design system component library. At build time, a bundler plugin
can scan every component's definitions, resolve references, and write a static
lookup index shipped with the MCP server package. When an agent calls
`searchComponents()`, the handler reads from that static structure — no scanning,
no resolution, no index construction per request.

The agent pays zero turn cost for the computation. The CI pipeline pays it
once. The result is faster responses, lower token cost per call, and no
variance in response time.

**When to apply it:**

| Computation | Runtime | Build time |
|---|---|---|
| Filtering by user input | ✓ | — |
| Counting available items | Runtime (`totalCount` field) | Build time (pre-count, embed in manifest) |
| Resolving references between definitions | — | ✓ (bundler plugin) |
| Indexing for search / BM25 | — | ✓ (write index to disk at build) |
| Building dependency graphs | — | ✓ (static graph serialised to JSON) |
| Generating tool output schemas | — | ✓ (schema library `toJsonSchema()` at registration) |

Build-time P4 is a design decision, not a code pattern — it shows up during
architecture planning, not implementation. Ask: "does this computation change
per-request, or is it stable across many requests?" Stable computation belongs
at build time.

---

## What it is

`michi` is a Rust crate of pure agentic response primitives — the formatting
and signalling conventions that make tools ergonomic for LLMs regardless of
protocol or language.

It encodes six of the ten [AXI principles](https://axi.md) as typed, tested
Rust: TOON list rendering, key-value single-item rendering, contextual
disclosure (`help[]`), content truncation, definitive empty states, structured
errors with exit codes, idempotency signals, retry delay primitives, and
content-first status responses.

The crate is intentionally narrow: **no protocol knowledge, no async runtime,
no CLI framework**. Pure computation — data in, strings and types out.
TypeScript consumers reach it via the NAPI npm wrapper `michi`. Rust
consumers take a direct crates.io or git dep.

---

## Name

**michi** — from 道 (Japanese: path, way, road).

The character 道 is the root of *dō* in martial arts and traditional arts:
judo, kendo, aikido, shodō, chadō. It means the path itself — and the act
of travelling it with intention. In the context of this crate, every `help[]`
block is michi: a marker that tells an agent which path to take next, with
what parameters.

Fits the suite's naming aesthetic: short real words borrowed from a specific
domain, with a metaphor that earns its place.

| Name | Origin | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Lumen | Latin | unit of luminous flux; light |
| Firkin | Middle English | small barrel; a measured unit |
| Monokl | Slavic / French | monocle; single-eye focus |
| Pulse | Latin | vital sign; rhythmic signal |
| **michi** | Japanese (道) | path, way, road |

---

## Organisation

GitHub org: **orin-axi** (`github.com/orin-axi`)

> "AXI" = Agent Experience Interface. The orin-axi org is the umbrella for
> tools designed to serve both human developers and AI agents as first-class
> users. `michi` is the primitive layer — the shared vocabulary of agent
> responses that all other tools in the suite can build on.

---

## Where michi fits in the suite

```
orin-axi suite
  michi           ← this crate; AXI response primitives
                    imported by any agent-facing tool
  Monokl          ← AST-based semantic code search
                    uses michi for --format toon output
  Firkin          ← barrel file generator
                    uses michi for structured error output
  Lumen           ← coding session analysis + ambient context
                    uses michi for status + hint primitives
  Pulse           ← code health intelligence
                    uses michi for toon list output
```

michi sits below every other tool in the suite as the shared primitive layer.
Non-agentic infrastructure tools (build scripts, formatters, etc.) never
encounter it — the package boundary enforces the separation.

---

## AXI principles encoded

| Principle | Module | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — TOON format | `toon` | Token-efficient list rendering (~40% vs JSON) |
| P2 — Minimal schemas | `kv` | Single-item KV rendering; field names appear once |
| P3 — Truncation | `truncate` | Size-bounded output with escape hatches |
| P4 — Aggregates | `toon`, `kv` | `totalCount` on every list/single-item response |
| P5 — Empty states | `empty` | Definitive `0 results` — never silent |
| P6 — Structured errors | `error` | `stdout` errors, typed exit codes, recovery hints |
| P7 — Ambient context | `status` | Content-first `StatusResponse` for no-arg invocations |
| P8 — Content first | `status` | `StatusResponse` — live state, not help text |
| P9 — Contextual disclosure | `hints` | `help[]` blocks with concrete next-step templates |
| Combined ops | `idempotency` | Already-done signals; partial success reporting |

Not encoded (caller's responsibility): P10 (consistent `--help`), combined
operation design, tiered schema loading.

---

## Namespaces

| Surface | Name |
|---|---|
| Rust crate (crates.io) | `michi` |
| npm package | `michi` |
| Rust module path | `michi::` |
| GitHub repo | `orin-axi/michi` |

## License

AGPL v3 (`AGPL-3.0-or-later`).

Rationale: viral copyleft is well-suited to CLI/library tools embedded in
pipelines. Creates natural friction against agentic services wrapping michi
commercially without contributing back. A CLA or contributor copyright
assignment clause per repo preserves future dual-licensing optionality.

6	## Overview
7	
8	`michi` is a Rust crate of pure agentic response primitives — the
9	conventions that make tools ergonomic for LLMs regardless of protocol or
10	language. It is general-purpose: useful to anyone building AXI-compliant
11	tools, not tied to any specific stack.
12	
13	It encodes six of the ten [AXI principles](https://axi.md) as typed, tested
14	Rust: TOON list rendering, key-value single-item rendering, contextual
15	disclosure (`help[]`), content truncation, definitive empty states, structured
16	errors with exit codes, idempotency signals, retry delay primitives, and
17	content-first status responses.
18	
19	The crate has no protocol knowledge (no MCP, no HTTP, no CLI framework) and
20	no async runtime dependency. It is pure computation: data in, strings and types
21	out. TypeScript consumers reach it via the NAPI npm wrapper `michi`. Rust
22	consumers take a direct crates.io or git dep.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Motivation
27	
28	AXI's 10 design principles describe how to build agent-ergonomic interfaces,
29	but the principles themselves are typically implemented ad-hoc — scattered as
30	implicit conventions in MCP servers, undocumented CLI output patterns, and
31	per-tool string formatting that drifts over time. When `michi` exists:
32	
33	- The TOON format has a canonical, tested Rust implementation shared by both
34	  MCP and CLI consumers
35	- `help[]` hint construction, `totalCount` formatting, truncation signals, and
36	  recovery hint shapes are defined once and cannot drift between consumers
37	- Any agent-facing Rust CLI can import the same primitives directly
38	- Any TypeScript MCP server or CLI can reach them via the NAPI npm package
39	
40	A non-agentic tool (infrastructure CLIs, build scripts) uses its own output
41	conventions and never encounters michi. The package boundary enforces the
42	separation — agentic concepts do not leak into infrastructure.
43

46	## Non-goals
47	
48	- **Display-format Markdown** — research-grounded LLM display formatters
49	  (fields, sections, tables) are the caller's concern. michi is the
50	  `audience: ["assistant"]` compact surface; display rendering for the
51	  `audience: ["user"]` surface stays in your MCP SDK or application layer.
52	- **MCP protocol knowledge** — no `content[]`, no `outputSchema`, no
53	  `structuredContent`. Those are assembled by the calling MCP framework.
54	- **CLI framework** — no argument parsing, no stdin/stdout handling. That
55	  belongs to the caller's CLI framework of choice.
56	- **HTTP client** — no auth handling, no request construction. michi
57	  provides retry delay primitives that a caller plugs into their own HTTP
58	  client.
59	- **Async runtime** — zero tokio, zero async-std. All functions are sync
60	  and pure. Callers own retry loops and timeout semantics.
61	- **Full retry implementation** — michi provides `RetryConfig`,
62	  `parse_retry_after()`, and `next_retry_delay()`. The actual retry loop
63	  (sleep + re-execute) stays in the caller.
64	- **Caching** — callers should use `moka` or equivalent. michi does not
65	  include a cache.
66	- **Logging / telemetry** — Rust consumers use the `tracing` crate
67	  independently.
68	- **Schema validation** — input validation is the caller's concern.
69	- **MCP server bootstrapping** — `server.tool()`, tool discovery, deferred
70	  loading. Protocol-specific, stays in your MCP SDK.

195	## TOON format specification
196	
197	TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) is the agent-facing list format.
198	It front-loads structure (type, count, field names) so the LLM has full
199	context before reading any row, then encodes rows as compact comma-separated
200	values. Field names appear once in the header rather than once per row.
201	
202	**Why TOON for lists?**
203	Standard JSON repeats field names on every item. Markdown key-value format
204	repeats field names per item, which is ideal for single items and small sets
205	but expensive at scale. TOON trades per-item field repetition for a one-time
206	header, saving proportionally more tokens as N grows. For lists of 5+ items,
207	TOON is the better token budget choice. For single items or small metadata
208	blocks, key-value format remains preferred — see `kv::render_kv()`.
209	
210	AXI's benchmark shows this class of output optimization delivers approximately
211	40% token reduction over equivalent JSON for list data.
212	
213	### Grammar
214	
215	```
216	document     ::= type_header NEWLINE row+ totalcount? help_block?
217	type_header  ::= type_name "[" count "]" "{" field_list "}" ":"
218	type_name    ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*                 (snake_case)
219	count        ::= [0-9]+                            (items in this response)
220	field_list   ::= field_name ("," field_name)*
221	field_name   ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*
222	row          ::= "  " value ("," value)* NEWLINE   (2-space indent)
223	value        ::= scalar | quoted
224	scalar       ::= [^,\n"]*
225	quoted       ::= '"' ( [^"\\] | "\\" . )* '"'     (for values with commas)
226	totalcount   ::= "totalCount: " [0-9]+ NEWLINE     (total available, may exceed count)
227	help_block   ::= "help[" [0-9]+ "]:" NEWLINE hint+
228	hint         ::= "  " [^\n]+ NEWLINE
229	```
230	
231	### Examples
232	
233	**List response:**
234	```
235	issues[3]{number,title,state}:
236	  42,Fix login redirect,open
237	  43,Add dark mode,open
238	  44,"Update deps, bump major",closed
239	totalCount: 47
240	help[2]:
241	  Call get_issue with number=<number> for full detail
242	  Call list_issues with state=open to filter
243	```
244	
245	**Truncated field value:**
246	```
247	components[2]{name,description,tokens}:
248	  Button,"Primary action element (148 chars truncated — use full=true)",12
249	  Icon,"Scalable vector icon (203 chars truncated — use full=true)",8
250	totalCount: 84
251	help[1]:
252	  Call get_component with name=<name> and full=true for complete description
253	```
254	
255	**Empty state:**
256	```
257	issues[0]{}:
258	totalCount: 0
259	help[1]:
260	  Try list_issues with a broader filter
261	```
262	
263	**Single recovery hint (no list):**
264	```
265	help[1]:
266	  Retry create_item with suggestedParams: { project: "PROJ", type: "Task" }
267	```
268	
269	### Escaping rules
270	
271	- Values containing commas MUST be quoted
272	- Values containing double-quote characters use backslash escape: `\"`
273	- Values containing newlines MUST be truncated before rendering — TOON
274	  does not support multi-line cell values
275	- Null/absent values render as empty scalar: `val1,,val3`
276	- Boolean values: `true` / `false` literals
277	- Numeric values: rendered without quotes

314	### `toon` — list rendering for N uniform-schema items
315	
316	TOON is the agent-facing format for lists. It front-loads structure (type,
317	count, field names) and encodes rows as compact comma-separated values.
318	Field names appear once in the header rather than once per row. Preferred
319	over key-value format for lists of 5+ items where token savings compound;
320	for single items, use `kv::render_kv()` instead.
321	
322	**Implementation note:** `render_toon()` pre-allocates output capacity via
323	`String::with_capacity` estimated from `items.len() × avg_row_estimate`.
324	This is the hot path — no intermediate allocations. The `escape.rs` submodule
325	handles comma/quote escaping inline without heap allocation for the common
326	case (no special characters).
327	
328	```rust
329	pub struct ToonOptions {
330	    /// Max cell value length before inline truncation.
331	    /// Appends "(N chars truncated — use full=true)" when exceeded.
332	    /// Default: 200
333	    pub max_cell_len: usize,
334	    /// Total items available. May exceed rows rendered.
335	    /// Emitted as "totalCount: N" line when Some.
336	    pub total_count: Option<u64>,
337	}
338	
339	impl Default for ToonOptions { ... }

347	/// Returns empty-state TOON when `items` is empty.
348	pub fn render_toon(
349	    type_name: &str,

482	### `error` — structured errors with exit codes
483	
484	AXI P6: errors go to stdout (not stderr), carry exit codes, carry hints,
485	and never block on interactive prompts. `AxiError` encodes this as a type.
486	
487	The HTTP status → ErrorCode mapping is NOT in michi — callers produce
488	an `ErrorCode` after interpreting whatever failure occurred. This keeps the
489	module free of HTTP knowledge.
490	
491	```rust
492	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
493	pub struct AxiError {
494	    pub code:        ErrorCode,
495	    pub message:     String,
496	    pub hints:       Vec<Hint>,
497	    pub recovery:    Option<RecoveryHint>,
498	    pub retryable:   bool,
499	    pub retry_after: Option<std::time::Duration>,
500	}
501	
502	impl std::fmt::Display for AxiError {
503	    // delegates to render()
504	}
505	
506	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
507	pub enum ErrorCode {
508	    // Non-retryable — agent should not retry without changing params
509	    InvalidInput,    // bad parameters
510	    NotFound,        // resource absent
511	    Unauthorized,    // auth failure
512	    Forbidden,       // permission denied
513	    Conflict,        // resource state mismatch
514	
515	    // Retryable — agent may retry same call
516	    RateLimited,     // 429 — check retry_after
517	    Unavailable,     // 503
518	    Timeout,         // request timed out
519	    ExternalFailure, // downstream error
520	}
521	
522	impl AxiError {
523	    pub fn new(code: ErrorCode, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self
524	    pub fn hint(mut self, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self
525	    pub fn recovery(mut self, r: RecoveryHint) -> Self
526	    pub fn retry_after(mut self, d: std::time::Duration) -> Self
527	
528	    /// Render to stdout-ready string with hints attached.
529	    pub fn render(&self) -> String
530	
531	    /// AXI exit codes: 0 = success/already_done, 1 = all other errors.
532	    /// Callers should not invent additional codes.
533	    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32
534	}
535	```

539	### `idempotency` — already-done signals and partial success
540	
541	Provides types and rendering for idempotency checks, already-done detection,
542	and partial-success reporting. The caller owns the persistence layer that
543	tracks what has been done; michi provides the rendering contract.

553	    pub fn from_hash(operation: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Self

557	/// Render an already-done response.
558	/// Exits 0 — this is a successful no-op, not an error.

560	pub fn already_done(

562	    summary: &str,
563	    hints: &[Hint],
564	) -> String

566	/// Partial success: some operations completed, some failed.

598	    pub max_delay:      std::time::Duration,
599	    pub backoff_factor: f64,
600	    pub jitter:         bool,
601	}
602	
603	impl Default for RetryConfig {
604	    fn default() -> Self {
605	        Self {
606	            max_attempts:   3,
607	            initial_delay:  std::time::Duration::from_secs(1),
608	            max_delay:      std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
609	            backoff_factor: 2.0,
610	            jitter:         true,
611	        }
612	    }
613	}
614	
615	/// Parse a Retry-After header value.
616	/// Accepts integer seconds ("120") or HTTP-date ("Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT").
617	/// Returns None for malformed or absent values.
618	pub fn parse_retry_after(value: &str) -> Option<std::time::Duration>
619	
620	/// Compute the next retry delay.
621	/// Applies exponential backoff, optional jitter, and clamps to max_delay.
622	/// Respects retry_after when provided — returns the larger of backoff and header.
623	/// Always returns at least initial_delay.
624	pub fn next_retry_delay(
625	    attempt: u32,
626	    config: &RetryConfig,
627	    retry_after: Option<std::time::Duration>,
628	) -> std::time::Duration
629	
630	/// Whether a status code is conventionally retryable.
631	/// Returns true for: 429, 502, 503, 504.
632	/// 500 is intentionally excluded — see supplement for rationale.
633	pub fn is_retryable_status(status: u16) -> bool
634	```
635	
636	Usage pattern for a caller implementing their own retry loop:
637	```rust
638	let config = RetryConfig::default();
639	for attempt in 0..config.max_attempts {
640	    match call_api() {
641	        Ok(result) => return Ok(result),
642	        Err(e) if michi::resilience::is_retryable_status(e.status) => {
643	            let retry_after = e.retry_after_header
644	                .and_then(|h| michi::resilience::parse_retry_after(&h));
645	            let delay = michi::resilience::next_retry_delay(attempt, &config, retry_after);
646	            sleep(delay).await;
647	        }
648	        Err(e) => return Err(e),
649	    }
650	}
651	```

724	### `response` — AgentResponse builder
725	
726	The primary integration point. Composes all modules into a single builder.
727	Callers use this rather than calling individual render functions directly.
728	
729	```rust
730	/// Builder for an agent-facing response. Routes to TOON or KV based on
731	/// which items method is called, not on item count.
732	///
733	/// # Format routing
734	/// - `.items()` called  → TOON (list of uniform-schema rows)
735	/// - `.kv_items()` called → KV  (single item or mixed-type metadata)
736	///
737	/// Use `.items()` for 5+ uniform rows. Use `.kv_items()` for single items,
738	/// status data, or heterogeneous metadata.
739	pub struct AgentResponse {
740	    type_name:      String,
741	    items:          Vec<Vec<Value>>,
742	    fields:         Vec<String>,
743	    single_item:    Vec<kv::KvItem>,
744	    total_count:    Option<u64>,
745	    hints:          Vec<Hint>,
746	    recovery:       Vec<RecoveryHint>,
747	    truncate_cells: usize,
748	}
749	
750	pub enum OutputFormat {
751	    /// TOON — token-efficient list format for audience:["assistant"]
752	    Toon,
753	    /// Markdown-KV — for single items and status
754	    Kv,
755	    /// Compact JSON — for structuredContent or client tooling
756	    Json,
757	}

759	impl AgentResponse {
760	    pub fn new(type_name: impl Into<String>) -> Self
761	
762	    // List path (→ TOON)
763	    pub fn items(mut self, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>, fields: &[&str]) -> Self
764	    pub fn total_count(mut self, n: u64) -> Self
765	
766	    // Single-item path (→ KV)
767	    pub fn kv_items(mut self, items: Vec<kv::KvItem>) -> Self
768	
769	    // Shared
770	    pub fn hint(mut self, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self
771	    pub fn hints(mut self, hints: Vec<Hint>) -> Self
772	    pub fn recovery_hint(mut self, r: RecoveryHint) -> Self
773	    pub fn truncate_cells_at(mut self, limit: usize) -> Self
774	
775	    pub fn render(&self, format: OutputFormat) -> String
776	    pub fn render_toon(&self) -> String       // shorthand → OutputFormat::Toon
777	    pub fn render_kv(&self) -> String         // shorthand → OutputFormat::Kv

877	## What michi provides vs what stays in your application
878	
879	### Formalising conventions that are typically implicit
880	
881	| Concept | Where it usually lives | Provided as |
882	|---|---|---|
883	| Contextual hints after output | Implicit strings per tool | `hints::Hint`, `render_hints()`, `append_hints()` |
884	| Total count on list responses | Number passed ad-hoc | `ToonOptions::total_count`, `totalCount:` line |
885	| Recovery hints on failure | Ad-hoc per server/tool | `recovery::RecoveryHint`, `render_recovery()` |
886	| Retry delay calculation | Inside caller's retry loop | `resilience::next_retry_delay()` |
887	| Retry-After header parsing | Ad-hoc string parsing | `resilience::parse_retry_after()` |
888	| Retryable status classification | Hardcoded booleans per caller | `resilience::is_retryable_status()` |
889	| Error classification shape | Ad-hoc per tool | `error::AxiError`, `error::ErrorCode` |
890	| Empty state handling | Ad-hoc per tool (often silent) | `empty::empty_state()` |
891	| Truncation | Ad-hoc per tool, no standard signal | `truncate::truncate()`, `truncate_inline()` |

895	| What | Why |
896	|---|---|
897	| TOON renderer | New format — token-efficient list encoding for agent context windows |

900	| `idempotency::already_done()` | Typed already-done signal with canonical output format |

941	## Performance contract
942	
943	| Operation | Target | Basis |
944	|---|---|---|
945	| `render_toon()` — 100 items, 4 fields | < 500µs | Simple string allocation, no I/O |
946	| `render_toon()` — 1000 items, 4 fields | < 3ms | Linear in N×fields |
947	| `render_kv()` — 10 items | < 20µs | Column-width scan + string join |
948	| `render_hints()` — 5 hints | < 10µs | Trivial string join |
949	| `truncate_inline()` | < 5µs | Single pass, char boundary safe |
950	| `parse_retry_after()` | < 2µs | String parse only |
951	| `next_retry_delay()` | < 1µs | Pure arithmetic |
952	| NAPI boundary overhead | < 5µs | Established from napi-rs benchmarks |
953	
954	**Allocation strategy:** `render_toon()` uses `String::with_capacity` estimated
955	from `items.len() × avg_row_estimate` before any writes. All functions are
956	allocation-bounded — no references held across call boundaries. The `escape.rs`
957	module avoids heap allocation for the common case (no special chars in a cell).
958	
959	**Thread safety:** All public functions are stateless pure functions.
960	`AgentResponse` is `Send + Sync` (all fields are owned, no interior
961	mutability). NAPI wrapper uses napi-rs safe threading model.
962	
963	Benchmarks via `criterion`. Run in CI on PRs touching `src/`.

1010	## Open questions
1011	
1012	**Q1 — TOON vs Markdown-KV for agent-facing list responses**
1013	AXI benchmarks the efficiency gains at the CLI/MCP level, but not the
1014	downstream LLM retrieval accuracy of TOON vs Markdown-KV for list data.
1015	Before treating TOON as universally superior for the `audience: ["assistant"]`
1016	surface, run a retrieval accuracy experiment: same list data, TOON vs
1017	Markdown-KV, retrieval task, across a few model sizes. If Markdown-KV wins
1018	on retrieval accuracy despite higher token cost, the right call for MCP
1019	consumers may be to use Markdown-KV even for lists. The crate ships either
1020	way — the question is which format callers should default to.
1021	
1022	**Q2 — External Rust consumer strategy**
1023	For external Rust binaries to depend on `michi`, options:
1024	(a) crates.io publish — cleanest for public consumers once API is stable
1025	(b) git dep with tag: `michi = { git = "https://github.com/orin-axi/michi", tag = "v0.x.y" }`
1026	    — good for early adopters before crates.io publish
1027	(c) private cargo registry — overhead not worth it
1028	
1029	Recommend (b) during development, (a) at first stable release. Gate
1030	crates.io publish behind at least one real consumer integration test.
1031	
1032	**Q3 — `cli` feature scope**
1033	Reserved for terminal-aware rendering. If `--format toon` in a human
1034	terminal context should wrap long rows or colourize the header, the `cli`
1035	feature is where that lives. Out of scope for v1 — michi v1 targets
1036	agent consumers only, not human-readable terminal output.
1037	
1038	**Q4 — `AgentResponse` builder vs standalone functions**
1039	The spec proposes both: low-level functions (`render_toon()`, `render_hints()`)
1040	and a high-level builder (`AgentResponse`). If the builder is the only
1041	thing NAPI-exported, the low-level functions are Rust-only. If both are
1042	exported, the NAPI surface grows. Recommend: export the builder and
1043	`renderHints()`/`appendHints()` only — low-level functions are implementation
1044	details available to Rust consumers.
1045	
1046	**Q5 — Recovery hint format**
1047	The current spec uses `serde_json::Value` for param values — type information
1048	is lost at the boundary. This is acceptable for display (agents read the
1049	rendered string) but may not be acceptable if `structuredContent` in an
1050	MCP context needs to carry typed recovery hints for client programmatic use.
1051	If so, `RecoveryHint` needs a more precise type model. Confirm scope before
1052	implementing.

1056	## Supplement — implementation notes and design rationale
1057	
1058	### `AgentResponse` format routing
1059	
1060	The builder routes to TOON or KV based on which items method the caller uses,
1061	not on item count. The caller is responsible for choosing the right format:
1062	
1063	```rust
1064	// List of uniform-schema items → TOON
1065	AgentResponse::new("issues")
1066	    .items(rows, &["number", "title", "state"])   // → render_toon()
1067	
1068	// Single item or mixed-type metadata → KV
1069	AgentResponse::new("issue")
1070	    .kv_items(vec![
1071	        KvItem { key: "number".into(), value: KvValue::Int(42) },
1072	        KvItem { key: "title".into(),  value: KvValue::Text("Fix login".into()) },
1073	    ])                                             // → render_kv()
1074	```
1075	
1076	Use `.items()` when all rows share the same schema and there are 5 or more of
1077	them. Use `.kv_items()` for single items, mixed-type status data, or any case
1078	where field names differ per row.
1079	
1080	---
1081	
1082	### `IdempotencyKey` — stable input serialisation
1083	
1084	`IdempotencyKey::from_hash(operation, data)` hashes the raw bytes of `data`.
1085	For the key to be canonical across calls with the same logical input, `data`
1086	must be produced deterministically:
1087	
1088	- **Maps and structs:** sort keys alphabetically before serialising to JSON.
1089	  `serde_json::to_vec` on a `HashMap` produces non-deterministic key order.
1090	  Use `BTreeMap` or a sorted intermediate representation.
1091	- **Floats:** avoid floating-point values in idempotency keys — representation
1092	  varies by architecture. Round to a fixed decimal or convert to integers.
1093	- **Timestamps:** exclude request-time fields (created_at, request_id) unless
1094	  the intent is a per-request key rather than a per-operation key.
1095	
1096	```rust
1097	// Correct: BTreeMap serialises with sorted keys
1098	let mut params: BTreeMap<&str, serde_json::Value> = BTreeMap::new();
1099	params.insert("project", json!("PROJ"));
1100	params.insert("type",    json!("Task"));
1101	let key = IdempotencyKey::from_hash("create_item", &serde_json::to_vec(&params)?);
1102	
1103	// Incorrect: HashMap key order is non-deterministic
1104	let params: HashMap<&str, _> = /* ... */;
1105	let key = IdempotencyKey::from_hash("create_item", &serde_json::to_vec(&params)?);
1106	// ^ same logical input may produce different keys on different calls
1107	```
1108	
1109	---
1110	
1111	### `is_retryable_status()` — why 500 is excluded
1112	
1113	The default retryable set is `{ 429, 502, 503, 504 }`. HTTP 500 (Internal
1114	Server Error) is intentionally absent.
1115	
1116	429 and 50x gateway errors (502, 503, 504) represent transient conditions
1117	where the same request is likely to succeed after a delay. 500 represents a
1118	server-side bug — retrying without changing the request will produce the same
1119	500. Worse, retrying write operations that returned 500 may produce duplicate
1120	side effects if the server processed the request before erroring.
1121	
1122	```rust
1123	// Default: 429, 502, 503, 504 only
1124	if is_retryable_status(status) { ... }
1125	
1126	// Custom: caller adds 500 for a specific API known to use it transiently
1127	let retryable = is_retryable_status(status) || status == 500;
1128	```
1129	
1130	---
1131	
1132	### `render_hints_only()` — the three-surface seam
1133	
1134	This method exists to support MCP frameworks that implement a three-surface
1135	response pattern: one content block for agent consumption
1136	(`audience: ["assistant"]`), one for display (`audience: ["user"]`), and a
1137	`structuredContent` payload for client tooling. In this pattern, the display
1138	body is rendered via the framework's own Markdown layer, while the agent-facing
1139	block combines TOON output with a `help[]` trailer.
1140	
1141	```typescript
1142	// Example: MCP framework TypeScript (simplified)
1143	function assembleToolResult(opts: RespondOpts): ToolResult {
1144	  const userBody      = renderDisplayMarkdown(opts.body);
1145	  const hintsBlock    = michi.renderHintsOnly(opts.hints);
1146	  const assistantBody = opts.assistant ?? (userBody + "\n" + hintsBlock);
1147	
1148	  return {
1149	    content: [
1150	      { type: "text", text: assistantBody,
1151	        annotations: { audience: ["assistant"], priority: 1.0 } },
1152	      { type: "text", text: userBody,
1153	        annotations: { audience: ["user"],      priority: 0.5 } },
1154	    ],
1155	    structuredContent: opts.structured ?? null,
1156	  };
1157	}
1158	```
1159	
1160	`render_hints_only()` is the narrow seam between michi and the calling
1161	framework's rendering layer — it allows the `help[]` format to be owned by
1162	Rust without requiring the framework to understand TOON.
1163	
1164	---
1165	
1166	### `parse_retry_after()` — format details
1167	
1168	Accepts either of the two forms defined in RFC 7231 §7.1.3:
1169	
1170	| Form | Example | Notes |
1171	|---|---|---|
1172	| Integer seconds | `"120"` | Seconds to wait from response time |
1173	| HTTP-date | `"Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT"` | Absolute datetime, UTC only |
1174	
1175	Returns `None` for any malformed value. `next_retry_delay()` internally
1176	clamps: the returned duration is always at least `config.initial_delay` and
1177	at most `config.max_delay`, regardless of what `parse_retry_after()` returns.
1178	
1179	---
1180	
1181	### `outputSchema` is in the LLM context
1182	
1183	A precision point that matters for token budget planning in MCP servers that
1184	use progressive disclosure or deferred tool loading:
1185	
1186	- **`outputSchema`** on a tool definition is part of `tools/list`. It IS
1187	  injected into the LLM context window at session start. It is a one-time
1188	  cost that amortises across the session as a prepaid reasoning contract.
1189	- **`structuredContent`** in a tool result is client-consumed only. It does
1190	  NOT enter the LLM context window.
1191	
1192	`outputSchema` should only be defined on always-loaded tools, or excluded from
1193	`tools/list` for deferred tools and supplied only when the tool is invoked.
1194	
1195	---
1196	
1197	### Build-time P4 — pre-computed aggregates at CI time
1198	
1199	AXI Principle 4 (pre-computed aggregates) applies at build time as well as
1200	runtime. Any deterministic computation that a tool needs repeatedly is a
1201	candidate for pre-computation in CI rather than per-request execution.
1202	
1203	**The pattern:** a build step scans definitions, resolves references, and
1204	writes a static lookup index shipped with the server package. When an agent
1205	calls the search tool, the handler reads from that static structure — no
1206	scanning, no resolution per request. The agent pays zero turn cost for the
1207	computation; CI pays it once.
1208	
1209	| Computation | Runtime | Build time |
1210	|---|---|---|
1211	| Filtering by user input | ✓ | — |
1212	| Counting available items | Runtime (`totalCount` field) | Build time (pre-count, embed in manifest) |
1213	| Resolving references between definitions | — | ✓ |
1214	| Indexing for search / BM25 | — | ✓ |
1215	| Building dependency graphs | — | ✓ |
1216	| Generating tool output schemas | — | ✓ (schema library `toJsonSchema()` at registration) |
1217

# michi — Specification
> orin-axi · Draft · June 2026

---

## Overview

`michi` is a Rust crate of pure agentic response primitives — the
conventions that make tools ergonomic for LLMs regardless of protocol or
language. It is general-purpose: useful to anyone building AXI-compliant
tools, not tied to any specific stack.

It encodes six of the ten [AXI principles](https://axi.md) as typed, tested
Rust: TOON list rendering, key-value single-item rendering, contextual
disclosure (`help[]`), content truncation, definitive empty states, structured
errors with exit codes, idempotency signals, retry delay primitives, and
content-first status responses.

The crate has no protocol knowledge (no MCP, no HTTP, no CLI framework) and
no async runtime dependency. It is pure computation: data in, strings and types
out. TypeScript consumers reach it via the NAPI npm wrapper `michi`. Rust
consumers take a direct crates.io or git dep.

---

## Motivation

AXI's 10 design principles describe how to build agent-ergonomic interfaces,
but the principles themselves are typically implemented ad-hoc — scattered as
implicit conventions in MCP servers, undocumented CLI output patterns, and
per-tool string formatting that drifts over time. When `michi` exists:

- The TOON format has a canonical, tested Rust implementation shared by both
  MCP and CLI consumers
- `help[]` hint construction, `totalCount` formatting, truncation signals, and
  recovery hint shapes are defined once and cannot drift between consumers
- Any agent-facing Rust CLI can import the same primitives directly
- Any TypeScript MCP server or CLI can reach them via the NAPI npm package

A non-agentic tool (infrastructure CLIs, build scripts) uses its own output
conventions and never encounters michi. The package boundary enforces the
separation — agentic concepts do not leak into infrastructure.

---

## Non-goals

- **Display-format Markdown** — research-grounded LLM display formatters
  (fields, sections, tables) are the caller's concern. michi is the
  `audience: ["assistant"]` compact surface; display rendering for the
  `audience: ["user"]` surface stays in your MCP SDK or application layer.
- **MCP protocol knowledge** — no `content[]`, no `outputSchema`, no
  `structuredContent`. Those are assembled by the calling MCP framework.
- **CLI framework** — no argument parsing, no stdin/stdout handling. That
  belongs to the caller's CLI framework of choice.
- **HTTP client** — no auth handling, no request construction. michi
  provides retry delay primitives that a caller plugs into their own HTTP
  client.
- **Async runtime** — zero tokio, zero async-std. All functions are sync
  and pure. Callers own retry loops and timeout semantics.
- **Full retry implementation** — michi provides `RetryConfig`,
  `parse_retry_after()`, and `next_retry_delay()`. The actual retry loop
  (sleep + re-execute) stays in the caller.
- **Caching** — callers should use `moka` or equivalent. michi does not
  include a cache.
- **Logging / telemetry** — Rust consumers use the `tracing` crate
  independently.
- **Schema validation** — input validation is the caller's concern.
- **MCP server bootstrapping** — `server.tool()`, tool discovery, deferred
  loading. Protocol-specific, stays in your MCP SDK.

---

## Consumer map

```
Any Rust CLI binary
  Cargo.toml dep on michi (crates.io or git)
  Render --format toon via michi::render_toon()
  Full access to all modules — no NAPI overhead

Any TypeScript CLI
  npm dep on michi
  --format toon dispatch calls into NAPI wrapper
  Same output; NAPI boundary is transparent

Any TypeScript MCP server
  npm dep on michi
  Renders TOON for audience:["assistant"] content block
  Assembles MCP content[] from the returned string
```

---

## Cargo.toml

```toml

version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

description = "AXI response primitives for agent-ergonomic tools"
license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"
repository = "https://github.com/orin-axi/michi"
keywords = ["axi", "agent", "mcp", "cli", "llm"]
categories = ["text-processing", "encoding", "development-tools"]

[features]
default = []
napi    = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]
cli     = []  # reserved: terminal-width-aware rendering, colour support

[dependencies]
serde      = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
thiserror  = "2"

[dependencies.napi]
version  = "2"
features = ["napi4"]
optional = true

[dependencies.napi-derive]
version  = "2"
optional = true

[build-dependencies.napi-build]
version  = "1"

[dev-dependencies]
criterion = { version = "0.5", features = ["html_reports"] }

[[bench]]

[[bench]]

  index.js                      # loadBinding + TS fallback
  index.d.ts                    # TypeScript types
  src/
