# michi — MVP Implementation Plan

> orin-axi · Draft · June 2026

---

## Overview

The MVP delivers the complete `michi` crate as specified in `docs/01-spec.md`:
all 11 modules, the `AgentResponse` builder, the NAPI npm wrapper, a full test
suite, and benchmarks. No features are deferred — v0.1.0 ships the complete
public API.

Implementation is split into 7 agent sessions across 5 phases. Sessions within
the same phase may run in parallel; the dependency graph enforces the ordering
between phases.

---

## Dependency graph

```text
Phase 0: Repository Setup           (1 session — must finish first)
    └─► Phase 1: Core Rendering     (2 sessions — parallel)
            └─► Phase 2: Primitives (2 sessions — parallel)
                    └─► Phase 3: Tests + NAPI  (2 sessions — parallel)
                            └─► Phase 4: Benchmarks + Polish (1 session)
```

---

## Phase summary

| Phase | Session | Depends on | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | S0 — Setup | — | Workspace, CI, stubs |
| 1 | S1A — Core Rendering | S0 | `toon`, `kv`, `hints` |
| 1 | S1B — Utilities | S0 | `truncate`, `empty`, `recovery` |
| 2 | S2A — Error + Resilience | S1A, S1B | `error`, `resilience` |
| 2 | S2B — Composition | S1A, S1B | `idempotency`, `status`, `response` |
| 3 | S3A — Tests | S2A, S2B | proptest + insta snapshots |
| 3 | S3B — NAPI | S2A, S2B | npm wrapper, Jest tests |
| 4 | S4 — Benchmarks + Polish | S3A, S3B | criterion, README, publish prep |

---

## Non-negotiable constraints (all sessions)

These rules apply to every file written in every session. No exceptions.

#### Rust

1. **Edition 2021, `rust-version = "1.93"`** — set in root `Cargo.toml`.
2. **No `unwrap()` or `expect()` in library code** — propagate all errors with
   `?`. Use `thiserror` for error types. `expect()` is only permitted in tests
   with a message explaining the invariant, and on infallible `writeln!` into a
   `String` (mark each such call with `// infallible`).
3. **No trait objects for dispatch** — no `Box<dyn Trait>` in hot paths. Use
   match arms or enum dispatch.
4. **No `unsafe` in this crate** — the only exception is inside the `#[napi]`

content.content:
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch/PR.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  # ── Rust ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked

  deny:
    name: Deny (licenses · advisories · bans)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  bench:
    name: Benchmarks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi 2>&1 | tee bench-results.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bench-results
          path: bench-results.txt

  # ── TypeScript ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  typescript:
    name: TypeScript / Node ${{ matrix.node }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["24", "26"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: "10"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

  # Verifies that npm and pnpm users get @oxc-react-docgen/napi automatically
  # as a transitive dep — no separate install step required.
  install:
    name: Install / Node ${{ matrix.node }} / ${{ matrix.pm }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["24", "26"]
        pm: [npm, pnpm]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: "10"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
      - run: pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin pack --out-dir /tmp/packed

      - name: Install via ${{ matrix.pm }}
        run: |
          mkdir /tmp/install-test && cd /tmp/install-test
          if [ "${{ matrix.pm }}" = "npm" ]; then
            npm install /tmp/packed/*.tgz
          else
            pnpm add /tmp/packed/*.tgz
          fi

      - name: Verify napi is a transitive dependency
        run: |
          node -e "
            const fs = require('fs');
            const base = '/tmp/install-test/node_modules';
            if (!fs.existsSync(base + '/@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin/package.json'))
              throw new Error('vite-plugin not installed');
            if (!fs.existsSync(base + '/@oxc-react-docgen/napi/package.json'))
              throw new Error('@oxc-react-docgen/napi not installed as transitive dep');
            console.log('OK');
          "

# oxc-react-docgen

10-100x faster drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON. See `docs/09-STATUS.md` for current phase and known bugs.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/CLAUDE.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/CLAUDE.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

content.content:
1	# Quality & Architecture Refactor Plan
2	
3	**Status:** Planning — not yet started  
4	**Prerequisites:** All existing 90 tests must stay green throughout  
5	**Goal:** A codebase that passes open-source scrutiny, not just CI
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Honest Diagnosis
10	
11	Before prescribing solutions, the actual problems:
12	
13	| File | Lines | Fns | Problem |
14	|------|-------|-----|---------|
15	| `resolver.rs` | 2,482 | 55 | Six unrelated concerns in one file |
16	| `extractor.rs` | 1,867 | 62 | One 1,800-line `impl` block |
17	| `types.rs` | 1,305 | 20 | Two abstraction layers + diagnostics all mixed |
18	| `cli/main.rs` | 760 | 14 | Five commands + config + output in `main.rs` |
19	
20	Beyond size, the specific code-level problems:
21	
22	1. **8-parameter functions** — `resolve_props_chain(type_name, type_args, consuming_file, mapping, ctx, visited, depth, diagnostics)`. Error-prone at call sites, impossible to add parameters without touching every caller.
23	
24	2. **`FxHashSet<String>` for the visited set** — heap allocates a `String` per visited type name. `CompactString` is already a workspace dep; most type names fit inline (≤24 bytes).
25	
26	3. **Silent IO failures** — `fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_default()` makes a permission error indistinguishable from an empty file. Users get 0 components, no diagnostic.
27	
28	4. **Hand-rolled serde for `PropType` and `CollectedType`** — written to work around a 19-minute compile time caused by serde derive recursion. Goes through `serde_json::Value` as an intermediate, allocating a heap value per prop during every serialization. Root cause: recursive enum variants weren't boxed. Fix is `Box<PropType>` on the `Array` variant (already done for `CollectedType`) and re-enabling derive.
29	
30	5. **`strip_json_comments` lives in `resolver.rs`** — a JSON utility function in the type resolver. Should be a crate or a `util` module.
31	
32	6. **`scoped_key` as raw `String`** — map keys are `format!("{}:{}", file_path, name)` constructed in multiple places. No type safety, no canonical constructor, compared by string equality everywhere.
33	
34	7. **Everything is `pub mod`** — `lib.rs` re-exports all eight modules. Consumers of the library crate can reach `extractor::SourceDataCollector`, `resolver::resolve_named`, `known::resolve_known` — all implementation details. The real public API is: `pipeline::{extract, PipelineOptions, WatchSession}`, `types::{ExtractionOutput, Diagnostic, DiagnosticSeverity}`, `react_types::{REACT_18, REACT_19}`.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Principles
39

125	## Behavioral Changes
126	
127	These are not cosmetic. Each one changes what the code does.
128	
129	### 1. `ResolveState` — the most load-bearing change
130	
131	Replaces the `visited`, `depth`, and `diagnostics` parameters threaded through every resolver function. Also adds `needed_specifiers` for cross-package resolution (see below).
132	
133	```rust
134	// resolver/state.rs
135	pub(crate) struct ResolveState {
136	    visited: FxHashSet<CompactString>,      // was FxHashSet<String>
137	    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
138	    depth: u8,
139	    /// Packages we needed but weren't in GlobalSourceData.
140	    /// Populated during resolution; consumed by the pipeline for cross-pkg loading.
141	    pub needed_specifiers: Vec<NeededSpecifier>,
142	}
143	
144	pub(crate) struct NeededSpecifier {
145	    pub package: String,            // e.g. "@radix-ui/react-primitive"
146	    pub from_file: Utf8PathBuf,     // the file that imported it
147	}
148	
149	impl ResolveState {
150	    pub fn new() -> Self { ... }
151	    
152	    /// Returns false if already visited (cycle detected).
153	    pub fn visit(&mut self, key: &str) -> bool {
154	        self.visited.insert(CompactString::from(key))
155	    }
156	    
157	    /// Returns None if depth limit exceeded (emits diagnostic automatically).
158	    pub fn descend(&mut self) -> Option<DepthGuard<'_>> { ... }
159	    
160	    pub fn note_needed(&mut self, package: String, from_file: Utf8PathBuf) {
161	        self.needed_specifiers.push(NeededSpecifier { package, from_file });
162	    }

164	```
165	
166	Every resolver function signature goes from 8 parameters to 4:
167	
168	```rust
169	// Before
170	fn resolve_props_chain(
171	    type_name: &str, type_args: &[String], consuming_file: &Utf8Path,
172	    mapping: &ComponentMapping, ctx: &ResolutionContext,
173	    visited: &mut FxHashSet<String>, depth: u8, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
174	) -> ResolvedChain
175	
176	// After
177	fn resolve_props_chain(
178	    type_name: &str, type_args: &[String],
179	    consuming_file: &Utf8Path, ctx: &ResolutionContext,
180	    state: &mut ResolveState,
181	) -> ResolvedChain
182	```
183	
184	### 2. `ScopedKey` newtype
185	
186	Map keys are currently `format!("{}:{}", file_path, name)` strings constructed in 6+ different places. A misformatted key silently produces a miss instead of an error.
187	
188	```rust
189	// types/global.rs
190	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Hash, Eq, PartialEq)]
191	pub(crate) struct ScopedKey(CompactString);
192	
193	impl ScopedKey {
194	    pub fn new(file: &Utf8Path, name: &str) -> Self {
195	        let mut s = CompactString::with_capacity(file.as_str().len() + 1 + name.len());
196	        s.push_str(file.as_str());
197	        s.push(':');
198	        s.push_str(name);
199	        Self(s)
200	    }
201	    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str { &self.0 }
202	}
203	```
204	
205	`GlobalSourceData` maps become `FxHashMap<ScopedKey, ...>` instead of `FxHashMap<String, ...>`. The compiler then enforces correct key construction everywhere.
206	
207	### 3. Proper IO error propagation
208	
209	```rust
210	// Before — permission error looks like empty file
211	let source = std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_default();
212	
213	// After — IO failures become diagnostics, not silent empties
214	match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
215	    Ok(source) => source,
216	    Err(e) => {
217	        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic::io_error(path, e));
218	        continue;
219	    }
220	}
221	```
222	
223	### 4. `PropType` serde — remove the intermediate `serde_json::Value`
224	
225	The hand-rolled impl was written because serde derive hit the recursion limit. The actual fix is `Box<PropType>` on recursive single-element variants. `Array` already uses `Box<PropType>`. The recursion comes from `Union(Vec<PropType>)` and `Intersection(Vec<PropType>)` — but `Vec<T>` doesn't recurse the serde macro (it uses a generic impl). The recursion comes from `Array(Box<PropType>)` being visited, which leads back to `PropType`.
226	
227	Profile this: try removing the manual impl and using `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` with the existing `Box<PropType>` on `Array`. If the recursion limit is still hit, increase `recursion_limit` — it's already set to 2048. The 19-minute compile was a serde 1.x codegen bug that is fixed in recent versions.
228	
229	If derive works: the intermediate `serde_json::Value` allocation goes away, the hand-rolled 200+ line impl goes away, and adding new variants to `PropType` stops requiring manual serde code.
230	
231	### 5. `FxHashSet<CompactString>` for visited
232	
233	One-line change, uses existing dep, eliminates heap allocation for the common case (most type names ≤24 bytes).
234	
235	### 6. Replace `strip_json_comments` with a crate
236	
237	```toml
238	# Cargo.toml
239	json-strip-comments = "1"    # or serde_json5 = "0.1"
240	```
241	
242	Remove the 20-line hand-written function from `resolver.rs`. This is in the wrong file regardless.
243

246	## Visibility Model
247	
248	**Public API surface** (what `lib.rs` exposes as `pub`):
249	
250	```rust
251	// lib.rs
252	pub mod pipeline;           // extract(), PipelineOptions, WatchSession
253	pub mod types {             // re-export only output types
254	    pub use crate::types_impl::output::*;
255	    pub use crate::types_impl::diagnostic::*;
256	}
257	pub mod react_types;        // REACT_18, REACT_19
258	
259	// Everything else is pub(crate):
260	pub(crate) mod extractor;
261	pub(crate) mod resolver;
262	pub(crate) mod known;
263	pub(crate) mod cache;
264	pub(crate) mod import_map;
265	pub(crate) mod types_impl;  // renamed from types to avoid collision
266	```
267	
268	**Within modules**, functions are `pub(crate)` if needed across modules, private otherwise. Nothing in `resolver/` or `extractor/` is `pub` unless it's `resolve_component` or `parse_file`.
269	
270	`cargo-semver-checks` in CI enforces this — if we accidentally expose an internal type in a future release, the check fails.
271	
272	---
273	
274	## Cross-Package Resolution
275	
276	Design established in prior sessions. Captures the key decisions here for context persistence.
277	
278	**Mechanism:** Import-guided, demand-driven, multi-pass.
279	
280	When `resolve_named` cannot find a type and can identify which import binding it came from (e.g., `Primitive` from `import { Primitive } from '@radix-ui/react-primitive'`), it calls `state.note_needed(package, from_file)` instead of (or in addition to) emitting a warning.
281	
282	After a resolution pass, `pipeline/resolve.rs` drains `state.needed_specifiers`, uses the already-present `ctx.oxc_resolver` to find each package's `.d.ts` entry point, parses them in parallel (same rayon pattern as Phase 1), merges into `GlobalSourceData` via `rcu`, and runs another resolution pass. Stops when frontier is empty or depth > 3 hops.
283	
284	**Nothing new to add to the workspace.** `oxc_resolver` is already wired into `ResolutionContext`. `DtsCache` already caches `.d.ts` parse results. `GlobalSourceData::merge()` already accepts new files. `parse_file()` already handles `.d.ts`. The loop in `pipeline/resolve.rs` is ~40 lines of wiring, not new machinery.
285	
286	**Stopping conditions:**
287	- Frontier is empty (all needed types resolved)
288	- Package already in `GlobalSourceData` (cycle / duplicate)
289	- Depth > 3 hops from original source files
290	- Package count added > 20 (safety valve)
291	- Package is in the known-React-types set (handled by `known.rs`, no file needed)
292	
293	**Opt-in config:**
294	```json
295	{ "followDeps": true }   // default: true when node_modules/ is accessible
296	{ "followDeps": false }  // explicit opt-out, strict single-package mode
297	{ "followDeps": ["@radix-ui/*", "@floating-ui/react"] }  // allowlist
298	```
299	
300	---
301	
302	## Tooling
303	
304	What actually matters for THIS codebase:
305	
306	**`.clippy.toml` — tighten thresholds to catch regressions:**
307	```toml
308	msrv = "1.94"
309	too-many-arguments-threshold = 5
310	too-many-lines-threshold = 80
311	cognitive-complexity-threshold = 20
312	```
313	
314	**`lib.rs` — promote key lints:**
315	```rust
316	#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]
317	#![warn(clippy::too_many_lines)]
318	#![allow(clippy::module_name_repetitions)]  // ResolvedChain in resolver/ is fine
319	#![allow(clippy::must_use_candidate)]       // too noisy for internal fns
320	#![allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]       // internal fns don't need this
321	```
322	
323	**`insta` snapshot tests** (already in workspace) — add before refactor starts. Lock the output format for every fixture. If any refactor step changes JSON output, the snapshot diff makes it visible immediately.
324	
325	**`divan` benchmarks** (already in workspace) — add baseline benchmarks for `parse_file`, `resolve_component`, and `extract` on representative fixtures before behavioral changes. After: verify no regression.
326	
327	**`proptest`** — property-based testing for the parser. Generate random valid-ish TypeScript strings and assert `parse_file` never panics. This is table stakes for a parser tool heading toward open source.
328	
329	**`cargo-semver-checks`** in CI — once the public API is locked down (visibility cleanup done), add to CI. Prevents accidental API surface expansion in releases.
330	
331	**`cargo-deny`** — add `deny.toml` for license policy (MIT/Apache-2.0 only) and to ban duplicate major versions of OXC crates (they must all be 0.135.x). OXC version skew causes subtle bugs.
332	
333	**What we are NOT doing:**
334	- `cargo-modules` — visualization only, doesn't enforce anything
335	- `phf` for `known.rs` — LLVM optimizes our 50-arm match; phf adds overhead
336	- Custom shell scripts for file length — the module split is the enforcement
337	- `cargo-machete`, `cargo-audit`, `cargo-bloat` — fine tools but none of them fix any of the identified problems
338	
339	---
340	
341	## Implementation Sequence
342	
343	Each phase keeps tests green. No skipping.
344	
345	### R1 — Add snapshot tests (before touching anything)
346	Add `insta` snapshot tests for every fixture's extraction output. These are the safety net for the entire refactor. ~1 day.
347	
348	### R2 — `types/` split
349	Split `types.rs` into `types/collected.rs`, `types/output.rs`, `types/diagnostic.rs`, `types/global.rs`. Introduce `ScopedKey`. Update all imports across the codebase. Pure structural — zero behavior change. Tests must stay green. ~1 day.
350	
351	### R3 — `ResolveState`
352	Introduce `resolver/state.rs`. Thread `ResolveState` through `resolve_component` and all callee functions, replacing `visited`, `depth`, `diagnostics` parameters. Change `FxHashSet<String>` to `FxHashSet<CompactString>` in the same pass. Tests must stay green. ~1 day.
353	
354	### R4 — `resolver/` module split
355	With `ResolveState` in place and cleaner function signatures, split `resolver.rs` into the module directory. Move `strip_json_comments` out (use a crate). Tests must stay green. ~1 day.
356	
357	### R5 — `extractor/` module split
358	Split `extractor.rs` into the module directory. Tests must stay green. ~half day.
359	
360	### R6 — `pipeline/` split + IO error propagation
361	Split `pipeline.rs`. Fix the `unwrap_or_default()` IO failures to emit diagnostics. ~half day.
362	
363	### R7 — CLI split
364	Split `cli/main.rs` into commands/. No behavioral change. ~half day.
365	
366	### R8 — Visibility cleanup
367	Change internal modules to `pub(crate)`. Establish the real public API in `lib.rs`. Add `cargo-semver-checks` to CI. ~half day.
368	
369	### R9 — `PropType` serde
370	Attempt `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` — if it works cleanly, remove the hand-rolled impl. If not, document why and move on. ~half day, possibly faster.
371	
372	### R10 — Cross-package resolution
373	With clean module structure and `ResolveState.needed_specifiers` in place, implement the multi-pass loop in `pipeline/resolve.rs`. ~1-2 days.
374	
375	### R11 — Tooling
376	`.clippy.toml` thresholds, `cargo-deny`, `cargo-semver-checks`, `proptest` for the parser. ~half day.
377	
378	---
379	
380	## What Does NOT Change
381	
382	- Data flow: `OXC parse → SourceData → GlobalSourceData → ComponentEntry → ExtractionOutput`
383	- All 90 existing unit tests
384	- The `known.rs` dispatch pattern (it's idiomatic and fast)
385	- The `DtsCache` implementation

# Quality & Architecture Refactor Plan

**Status:** Planning — not yet started  
**Prerequisites:** All existing 90 tests must stay green throughout  
**Goal:** A codebase that passes open-source scrutiny, not just CI

---

## Honest Diagnosis

Before prescribing solutions, the actual problems:

| File | Lines | Fns | Problem |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `resolver.rs` | 2,482 | 55 | Six unrelated concerns in one file |
| `extractor.rs` | 1,867 | 62 | One 1,800-line `impl` block |
| `types.rs` | 1,305 | 20 | Two abstraction layers + diagnostics all mixed |
| `cli/main.rs` | 760 | 14 | Five commands + config + output in `main.rs` |

Beyond size, the specific code-level problems:

1. **8-parameter functions** — `resolve_props_chain(type_name, type_args, consuming_file, mapping, ctx, visited, depth, diagnostics)`. Error-prone at call sites, impossible to add parameters without touching every caller.

2. **`FxHashSet<String>` for the visited set** — heap allocates a `String` per visited type name. `CompactString` is already a workspace dep; most type names fit inline (≤24 bytes).

3. **Silent IO failures** — `fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_default()` makes a permission error indistinguishable from an empty file. Users get 0 components, no diagnostic.

4. **Hand-rolled serde for `PropType` and `CollectedType`** — written to work around a 19-minute compile time caused by serde derive recursion. Goes through `serde_json::Value` as an intermediate, allocating a heap value per prop during every serialization. Root cause: recursive enum variants weren't boxed. Fix is `Box<PropType>` on the `Array` variant (already done for `CollectedType`) and re-enabling derive.

5. **`strip_json_comments` lives in `resolver.rs`** — a JSON utility function in the type resolver. Should be a crate or a `util` module.

6. **`scoped_key` as raw `String`** — map keys are `format!("{}:{}", file_path, name)` constructed in multiple places. No type safety, no canonical constructor, compared by string equality everywhere.

7. **Everything is `pub mod`** — `lib.rs` re-exports all eight modules. Consumers of the library crate can reach `extractor::SourceDataCollector`, `resolver::resolve_named`, `known::resolve_known` — all implementation details. The real public API is: `pipeline::{extract, PipelineOptions, WatchSession}`, `types::{ExtractionOutput, Diagnostic, DiagnosticSeverity}`, `react_types::{REACT_18, REACT_19}`.

---

## Principles

**The module split is the enforcement mechanism, not a tool on top.** Once `resolver.rs` becomes `resolver/mod.rs + chain.rs + alias.rs + import.rs + html.rs`, you cannot recreate a 2,500-line resolver file without actively fighting the structure. No shell script needed.

**Structural and behavioral changes together.** Moving code between files without fixing the design problems just moves the mess around. The behavioral changes (ResolveState, ScopedKey, error propagation, serde) are equally important and should happen alongside the structural split, not after.

**Tests are the safety net.** The 90 existing tests define correct behavior. Every refactor step must keep them green. The `insta` snapshot tests (already a workspace dep) should be added before the refactor starts to lock in output format.

**Clippy at the right thresholds catches regressions.** Configure `.clippy.toml` with `too-many-arguments-threshold = 5` and `too-many-lines-threshold = 80` so that the violations we fix today can't creep back in.

---

## Module Structure (Target)

  alias.rs              — classify_type_alias (Omit/Pick/Passthrough/Union/Intersection)

  visit.rs              — impl Visit for SourceDataCollector (AST walker entry points)
  defaults.rs           — extract_param_defaults, destructure default extraction

resolver/

## Behavioral Changes

These are not cosmetic. Each one changes what the code does.

### 1. `ResolveState` — the most load-bearing change

Replaces the `visited`, `depth`, and `diagnostics` parameters threaded through every resolver function. Also adds `needed_specifiers` for cross-package resolution (see below).

```rust
// resolver/state.rs
pub(crate) struct ResolveState {
    visited: FxHashSet<CompactString>,      // was FxHashSet<String>
    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    depth: u8,
    /// Packages we needed but weren't in GlobalSourceData.
    /// Populated during resolution; consumed by the pipeline for cross-pkg loading.
    pub needed_specifiers: Vec<NeededSpecifier>,
}

pub(crate) struct NeededSpecifier {
    pub package: String,            // e.g. "@radix-ui/react-primitive"
    pub from_file: Utf8PathBuf,     // the file that imported it
}

impl ResolveState {
    pub fn new() -> Self { ... }
    
    /// Returns false if already visited (cycle detected).
    pub fn visit(&mut self, key: &str) -> bool {
        self.visited.insert(CompactString::from(key))
    }
    
    /// Returns None if depth limit exceeded (emits diagnostic automatically).
    pub fn descend(&mut self) -> Option<DepthGuard<'_>> { ... }
    
    pub fn note_needed(&mut self, package: String, from_file: Utf8PathBuf) {
        self.needed_specifiers.push(NeededSpecifier { package, from_file });
    }
}
```

Every resolver function signature goes from 8 parameters to 4:

```rust
// Before
fn resolve_props_chain(
    type_name: &str, type_args: &[String], consuming_file: &Utf8Path,
    mapping: &ComponentMapping, ctx: &ResolutionContext,
    visited: &mut FxHashSet<String>, depth: u8, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
) -> ResolvedChain

// After
fn resolve_props_chain(
    type_name: &str, type_args: &[String],
    consuming_file: &Utf8Path, ctx: &ResolutionContext,
    state: &mut ResolveState,
) -> ResolvedChain
```

### 2. `ScopedKey` newtype

Map keys are currently `format!("{}:{}", file_path, name)` strings constructed in 6+ different places. A misformatted key silently produces a miss instead of an error.

```rust
// types/global.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Hash, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct ScopedKey(CompactString);

impl ScopedKey {
    pub fn new(file: &Utf8Path, name: &str) -> Self {
        let mut s = CompactString::with_capacity(file.as_str().len() + 1 + name.len());
        s.push_str(file.as_str());
        s.push(':');
        s.push_str(name);
        Self(s)
    }
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str { &self.0 }
}
```

`GlobalSourceData` maps become `FxHashMap<ScopedKey, ...>` instead of `FxHashMap<String, ...>`. The compiler then enforces correct key construction everywhere.

### 3. Proper IO error propagation

```rust
// Before — permission error looks like empty file
let source = std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_default();

// After — IO failures become diagnostics, not silent empties
match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
    Ok(source) => source,
    Err(e) => {
        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic::io_error(path, e));
        continue;
    }
}
```

### 4. `PropType` serde — remove the intermediate `serde_json::Value`

The hand-rolled impl was written because serde derive hit the recursion limit. The actual fix is `Box<PropType>` on recursive single-element variants. `Array` already uses `Box<PropType>`. The recursion comes from `Union(Vec<PropType>)` and `Intersection(Vec<PropType>)` — but `Vec<T>` doesn't recurse the serde macro (it uses a generic impl). The recursion comes from `Array(Box<PropType>)` being visited, which leads back to `PropType`.

Profile this: try removing the manual impl and using `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` with the existing `Box<PropType>` on `Array`. If the recursion limit is still hit, increase `recursion_limit` — it's already set to 2048. The 19-minute compile was a serde 1.x codegen bug that is fixed in recent versions.

If derive works: the intermediate `serde_json::Value` allocation goes away, the hand-rolled 200+ line impl goes away, and adding new variants to `PropType` stops requiring manual serde code.

### 5. `FxHashSet<CompactString>` for visited

One-line change, uses existing dep, eliminates heap allocation for the common case (most type names ≤24 bytes).

### 6. Replace `strip_json_comments` with a crate

```toml
# Cargo.toml
json-strip-comments = "1"    # or serde_json5 = "0.1"
```

Remove the 20-line hand-written function from `resolver.rs`. This is in the wrong file regardless.

---

## Visibility Model

**Public API surface** (what `lib.rs` exposes as `pub`):

```rust
// lib.rs
pub mod pipeline;           // extract(), PipelineOptions, WatchSession
pub mod types {             // re-export only output types
    pub use crate::types_impl::output::*;
    pub use crate::types_impl::diagnostic::*;
}
pub mod react_types;        // REACT_18, REACT_19

// Everything else is pub(crate):
pub(crate) mod extractor;
pub(crate) mod resolver;
pub(crate) mod known;
pub(crate) mod cache;
pub(crate) mod import_map;
pub(crate) mod types_impl;  // renamed from types to avoid collision
```

**Within modules**, functions are `pub(crate)` if needed across modules, private otherwise. Nothing in `resolver/` or `extractor/` is `pub` unless it's `resolve_component` or `parse_file`.

`cargo-semver-checks` in CI enforces this — if we accidentally expose an internal type in a future release, the check fails.

---

## Cross-Package Resolution

Design established in prior sessions. Captures the key decisions here for context persistence.

**Mechanism:** Import-guided, demand-driven, multi-pass.

When `resolve_named` cannot find a type and can identify which import binding it came from (e.g., `Primitive` from `import { Primitive } from '@radix-ui/react-primitive'`), it calls `state.note_needed(package, from_file)` instead of (or in addition to) emitting a warning.

After a resolution pass, `pipeline/resolve.rs` drains `state.needed_specifiers`, uses the already-present `ctx.oxc_resolver` to find each package's `.d.ts` entry point, parses them in parallel (same rayon pattern as Phase 1), merges into `GlobalSourceData` via `rcu`, and runs another resolution pass. Stops when frontier is empty or depth > 3 hops.

**Nothing new to add to the workspace.** `oxc_resolver` is already wired into `ResolutionContext`. `DtsCache` already caches `.d.ts` parse results. `GlobalSourceData::merge()` already accepts new files. `parse_file()` already handles `.d.ts`. The loop in `pipeline/resolve.rs` is ~40 lines of wiring, not new machinery.

**Stopping conditions:**
- Frontier is empty (all needed types resolved)
- Package already in `GlobalSourceData` (cycle / duplicate)
- Depth > 3 hops from original source files
- Package count added > 20 (safety valve)
- Package is in the known-React-types set (handled by `known.rs`, no file needed)

**Opt-in config:**
```json
{ "followDeps": true }   // default: true when node_modules/ is accessible
{ "followDeps": false }  // explicit opt-out, strict single-package mode
{ "followDeps": ["@radix-ui/*", "@floating-ui/react"] }  // allowlist
```

---

## Tooling

What actually matters for THIS codebase:

**`.clippy.toml` — tighten thresholds to catch regressions:**
```toml
msrv = "1.94"
too-many-arguments-threshold = 5
too-many-lines-threshold = 80
cognitive-complexity-threshold = 20
```

**`lib.rs` — promote key lints:**
```rust
#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]
#![warn(clippy::too_many_lines)]
#![allow(clippy::module_name_repetitions)]  // ResolvedChain in resolver/ is fine
#![allow(clippy::must_use_candidate)]       // too noisy for internal fns
#![allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]       // internal fns don't need this
```

**`insta` snapshot tests** (already in workspace) — add before refactor starts. Lock the output format for every fixture. If any refactor step changes JSON output, the snapshot diff makes it visible immediately.

**`divan` benchmarks** (already in workspace) — add baseline benchmarks for `parse_file`, `resolve_component`, and `extract` on representative fixtures before behavioral changes. After: verify no regression.

**`proptest`** — property-based testing for the parser. Generate random valid-ish TypeScript strings and assert `parse_file` never panics. This is table stakes for a parser tool heading toward open source.

**`cargo-semver-checks`** in CI — once the public API is locked down (visibility cleanup done), add to CI. Prevents accidental API surface expansion in releases.

**`cargo-deny`** — add `deny.toml` for license policy (MIT/Apache-2.0 only) and to ban duplicate major versions of OXC crates (they must all be 0.135.x). OXC version skew causes subtle bugs.

**What we are NOT doing:**
- `cargo-modules` — visualization only, doesn't enforce anything
- `phf` for `known.rs` — LLVM optimizes our 50-arm match; phf adds overhead
- Custom shell scripts for file length — the module split is the enforcement
- `cargo-machete`, `cargo-audit`, `cargo-bloat` — fine tools but none of them fix any of the identified problems

---

## Implementation Sequence

Each phase keeps tests green. No skipping.

### R1 — Add snapshot tests (before touching anything)
Add `insta` snapshot tests for every fixture's extraction output. These are the safety net for the entire refactor. ~1 day.

### R2 — `types/` split
Split `types.rs` into `types/collected.rs`, `types/output.rs`, `types/diagnostic.rs`, `types/global.rs`. Introduce `ScopedKey`. Update all imports across the codebase. Pure structural — zero behavior change. Tests must stay green. ~1 day.

### R3 — `ResolveState`
Introduce `resolver/state.rs`. Thread `ResolveState` through `resolve_component` and all callee functions, replacing `visited`, `depth`, `diagnostics` parameters. Change `FxHashSet<String>` to `FxHashSet<CompactString>` in the same pass. Tests must stay green. ~1 day.

### R4 — `resolver/` module split
With `ResolveState` in place and cleaner function signatures, split `resolver.rs` into the module directory. Move `strip_json_comments` out (use a crate). Tests must stay green. ~1 day.

### R5 — `extractor/` module split
Split `extractor.rs` into the module directory. Tests must stay green. ~half day.

### R6 — `pipeline/` split + IO error propagation
Split `pipeline.rs`. Fix the `unwrap_or_default()` IO failures to emit diagnostics. ~half day.

### R7 — CLI split
Split `cli/main.rs` into commands/. No behavioral change. ~half day.

### R8 — Visibility cleanup
Change internal modules to `pub(crate)`. Establish the real public API in `lib.rs`. Add `cargo-semver-checks` to CI. ~half day.

### R9 — `PropType` serde
Attempt `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` — if it works cleanly, remove the hand-rolled impl. If not, document why and move on. ~half day, possibly faster.

### R10 — Cross-package resolution
With clean module structure and `ResolveState.needed_specifiers` in place, implement the multi-pass loop in `pipeline/resolve.rs`. ~1-2 days.

### R11 — Tooling
`.clippy.toml` thresholds, `cargo-deny`, `cargo-semver-checks`, `proptest` for the parser. ~half day.

---

## What Does NOT Change

- Data flow: `OXC parse → SourceData → GlobalSourceData → ComponentEntry → ExtractionOutput`
- All 90 existing unit tests
- The `known.rs` dispatch pattern (it's idiomatic and fast)
- The `DtsCache` implementation
- The `import_map.rs` implementation
- The `react_types.rs` data tables
- The `ArcSwap` + rayon parallel resolution (already correct)
- The NAPI and CLI public interfaces
- The output JSON format (guarded by snapshot tests)

content.text:
Good — got everything I need. oxc-react-codegen is the template. Here's the full synthesis across every area you raised:

---

## Crate selection: Rayon, miette, tokio?

**None of them belong in michi core.** Here's why:

- **Rayon** — parallelism for data-processing pipelines. michi has nothing to parallelize: `render_toon()` for 100 rows is <500µs, sequential, pure string building. Rayon would add a thread pool to a crate that does no I/O and holds no state.
- **miette** — beautiful human-readable diagnostic display. michi's errors (`AxiError`) are *agent-facing* — compact stdout strings, not terminal diagnostics. miette is for the human display surface michi explicitly excludes. Keep thiserror only.
- **tokio** (that's "taikio") — the spec says it explicitly: zero async. michi is pure sync. Callers own retry loops and sleep.

**What michi does need, derived from oxc patterns:**

| Dep | Why |
|---|---|
| `thiserror = "2"` | AxiError derives `std::error::Error` |
| `serde` + `serde_json = "1"` | RecoveryHint params, `render_json()` output |
| `sha2 = "^0.10"` | `IdempotencyKey::from_hash` — RustCrypto, zero transitive deps |
| `napi = "3"`, `napi-derive = "3"` | NAPI wrapper — **not v2, the spec is behind** |

Dev only:

| Dep | Why |
|---|---|
| `divan = "0.1"` | Benchmarks — **not criterion**, this is the current standard |
| `insta = { version = "1", features = ["yaml"] }` | Snapshot tests |
| `proptest = "1"` | Grammar conformance, truncation, retry |

---

## Lint, test, coverage, benchmarks

Straight from oxc-react-codegen's patterns:

**Test runner:** `cargo nextest` (parallel, faster, better output than `cargo test`). All CI test jobs use `taiki-e/install-action@nextest`.

**Coverage:** `cargo-llvm-cov nextest` via `taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov`. Outputs `lcov.info`, uploaded to Codecov. Run on every PR.

**Benchmarks:** `divan` (not criterion). Run on `main` pushes only — not on PRs. Emit results as a CI artifact for comparison. The spec's performance targets (<500µs for 100 rows, <3ms for 1000 rows) become divan assertions.

**Lint stack:**
- `cargo fmt --check` — rustfmt with `max_width = 120`, `use_small_heuristics = "Max"`
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` — `.clippy.toml`:
  ```toml
  msrv = "1.93"
  too-many-arguments-threshold = 5
  too-many-lines-threshold = 150
  ```
- `cargo deny` — `deny.toml` with license allowlist (AGPL, MIT, Apache-2.0, ISC, BSD-*) and ban on duplicate major versions
- `typos` — spell checking, with a `.typos.toml` for domain exceptions (toon, axi, napi, michi)

**Toolchain pinning:** `rust-toolchain.toml` at repo root pinning a specific stable version (1.93+ per spec MSRV). This makes CI deterministic.

---

## Architecture — what changes from the spec

The 11-module design is correct. One structural decision to firm up: **single crate at the workspace root, NAPI wrapper as a sibling crate**.

```
michi/                          ← workspace root (also the lib crate)
  Cargo.toml                    ← [workspace] + [package] in one file
  rust-toolchain.toml
  build.rs                      ← napi-build conditional on feature
  .rustfmt.toml
  .clippy.toml
  .typos.toml
  deny.toml
  CLAUDE.md
  README.md
  src/
    lib.rs
    toon/
      mod.rs
      escape.rs
      render.rs
    kv/mod.rs
    hints.rs, truncate.rs, empty.rs
    error.rs, idempotency.rs
    resilience.rs, status.rs, recovery.rs
    response.rs
    napi.rs                     ← #[napi] feature-gated
  benches/
    toon_render.rs              ← divan, not criterion
    kv_render.rs
  tests/
    toon_integration.rs, kv_integration.rs
    resilience_integration.rs, idempotency_integration.rs
    snapshot_tests.rs
  packages/
    michi-node/                 ← NAPI npm package (crate + package.json)
      Cargo.toml
      package.json              ← name: "michi"
      index.js                  ← platform loadBinding
      index.d.ts                ← auto-generated by napi-derive v3 (not hand-written!)
      src/lib.rs
      __test__/index.test.mjs
  .github/workflows/
    ci.yml
  docs/
    00-overview.md
    01-spec.md
    projects/
      01-mvp.md
      agents/                   ← session briefs (see below)
        S0-setup.md
        S1A-toon-kv-hints.md
        S1B-truncate-empty-recovery.md
        S2A-error-resilience.md
        S2B-idempotency-status-response.md
        S3A-tests.md
        S3B-napi.md
        S4-benchmarks-polish.md
```

**NAPI v3 note:** `napi-derive 3.x` auto-generates `index.d.ts` from `#[napi]` annotations — no hand-written types file. The spec's hand-written `index.d.ts` becomes a generated artifact, committed to the repo. This is a meaningful improvement over what the spec describes.

**CLI usage:** michi has no binary. When a Rust CLI tool (Monokl, Firkin, etc.) wants `--format toon`, it calls `michi::render_toon()` or uses the `AgentResponse` builder. The consuming CLI owns the flag parsing and dispatch. The `cli` feature flag is reserved for v2 terminal-aware rendering (colors, line-wrap).

**MCP usage:** TypeScript MCP servers `import { AgentResponse } from 'michi'` and call `.renderToon()`. The NAPI wrapper makes this transparent. A usage example lives in the spec; an actual example MCP server is out of scope for this crate.

**Parallelization:** None in michi itself. The rendering functions are pure, fast, and synchronous. Parallelism in consuming tools is their concern.

---

## CLAUDE.md design

```markdown
# michi

AXI response primitives — canonical TOON renderer, KV renderer, hint blocks,
and structured errors for agent-facing tools. Part of the orin-axi suite.

See docs/01-spec.md for the full specification.

## Commands

cargo nextest run                      # tests (all modules)
cargo clippy -- -D warnings            # lint
cargo bench                            # benchmarks (divan)
cargo insta review                     # review pending snapshots

## Non-negotiables

1. No unwrap() in library code — use ? or mark // infallible on writeln!
2. String::with_capacity before every render loop — hot path, no exceptions
3. Char boundaries only — never slice str at byte offsets in truncation
4. All pub items have doc comments — pub struct, pub fn, pub enum
5. No async, no tokio, no rayon — pure sync, zero runtime deps
6. No unsafe except inside #[napi] boundary (napi-derive manages it)
7. BTreeMap for anything in rendered output — deterministic key order

## Architecture

11 pure-computation modules. Data in → strings and types out. No I/O.

  toon/      — TOON list renderer (P1); escape.rs + render.rs
  kv/        — Markdown-KV single-item renderer (P1)
  hints.rs   — help[] block construction (P9)
  truncate.rs — char-boundary-safe truncation (P3)
  empty.rs   — definitive zero states (P5)
  error.rs   — AxiError + ErrorCode, stdout errors, exit codes (P6)
  idempotency.rs — already_done(), PartialSuccess (P6)
  resilience.rs  — RetryConfig, parse_retry_after(), next_retry_delay()
  status.rs  — StatusResponse, content-first orientation (P8)
  recovery.rs — RecoveryHint, render_recovery()
  response.rs — AgentResponse builder — the main integration point

packages/michi-node/ — NAPI npm wrapper (npm: michi)
```

---

## Local agents — session brief documents

Each worktree session gets a standalone brief in `docs/projects/agents/`. These are what a Claude Code session receives to start work. Each brief contains:

- **Mission** — one sentence
- **Reads** — which spec sections are authoritative
- **Produces** — exact list of files to write/modify
- **Acceptance criteria** — what `cargo nextest run`, `cargo clippy` must output
- **Non-negotiables** — links to the global list in CLAUDE.md
- **Gotchas** — session-specific traps (NAPI builder pattern, unicode truncation, etc.)
- **Does NOT touch** — explicit list of out-of-scope files

The S0 session brief also includes the CLAUDE.md content to write, the tooling config files, and the CI workflow — so later sessions start in a fully configured repo.

---

## Key decision I need from you before writing the design doc

One thing I want to confirm: **the spec currently has the NAPI wrapper in `packages/michi-node/` as a separate Cargo crate that wraps the root crate.** That's the "dual-crate" pattern. The alternative (used by some napi-rs projects) is to have `napi.rs` in the main crate gated behind the `napi` feature — a single-crate pattern.

Dual-crate (`packages/michi-node/` wraps `michi`) is cleaner for publishing — the Rust crate and the npm package have independent Cargo.tomls and neither leaks the other's build deps. It's what oxc-react-codegen does.

Single-crate (feature flag in `michi` itself) is simpler but `napi-build` ends up as a build-dep on the library crate, which is awkward for Rust-only consumers.

**My recommendation: dual-crate as the spec describes.** Confirm and I'll write the design doc and then move to session briefs.

content.text:
This is the key architectural insight that changes the scope of michi. Let me think through it properly.

---

## The AXI workflow insight

The thesis: agents are expensive at the turn level. Every back-and-forth costs context, latency, and money. An agent calling `get_pr`, then `get_checks`, then `get_comments`, then `analyze_diff` — four turns — is AXI anti-pattern. A single `review_pr` workflow tool that does all four internally and returns a synthesized response is one turn. **The leverage point is the workflow, not the individual operation.**

michi's current scope only helps with the *response format* of individual operations. It has no vocabulary for representing *workflow state* — multi-step progress, parallel step groups, compound results that synthesize multiple API calls.

---

## What this means architecturally

michi stays pure computation (no execution, no async, no I/O). But it should gain a **`pipeline` module** that provides the representation and rendering layer for workflow-level responses, exactly like how `resilience` gives you `next_retry_delay()` but not the retry loop.

The consumer executes the steps (possibly in parallel with rayon/tokio/whatever), then hands michi an assembled `Pipeline` to render. michi's job: canonical, compact, agent-readable output for multi-step state.

**Proposed `pipeline` module:**

```rust
pub struct Pipeline {
    pub name: String,
    pub steps: Vec<StepGroup>,   // groups allow parallel vs sequential modeling
    pub hints: Vec<Hint>,
}

pub struct StepGroup {
    pub mode: GroupMode,          // Sequential | Parallel
    pub steps: Vec<Step>,
}

pub enum GroupMode { Sequential, Parallel }

pub struct Step {
    pub name: String,
    pub status: StepStatus,
    pub summary: Option<String>,  // one-line result for compact view
    pub output: Option<String>,   // full TOON/KV blob (shown in verbose mode)
    pub error: Option<AxiError>,
}

pub enum StepStatus { Pending, Running, Done, Skipped, Failed }

impl Pipeline {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self
    pub fn step(mut self, step: Step) -> Self           // adds to sequential group
    pub fn parallel(mut self, steps: Vec<Step>) -> Self // adds a parallel group
    pub fn hint(mut self, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self
    pub fn render(&self) -> String                      // compact TOON table
    pub fn render_verbose(&self) -> String              // includes per-step output blobs
    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32                      // 0 = all done/skipped, 1 = any failed
}
```

**The compact render format (TOON-compatible):**

```
pipeline[5]{step,status,summary}:
  validate_input,done,"Schema OK"
  fetch_pr,done,"PR #42 — 3 files changed"
  fetch_checks,done,"3/3 passing"
  post_review,failed,"Unauthorized — check token scope"
  notify_team,skipped,""
progress: 3 done · 1 failed · 1 skipped
help[1]:
  Retry post_review after fixing token scope — all prior steps already complete
```

This is standard TOON with `pipeline` as the type name, plus a `progress:` summary line — one new line type in the grammar.

**Parallel group render:**

```
pipeline[6]{step,status,summary}:
  [parallel]
  fetch_pr,done,"PR #42"
  fetch_checks,done,"3/3 passing"
  fetch_diff,done,"847 lines changed"
  [sequential]
  analyze,done,"2 potential issues found"
  post_comment,pending,""
  request_review,pending,""
progress: 4/6
```

The `[parallel]` / `[sequential]` group headers are new grammar productions that agents learn to parse.

---

## How this connects to existing modules

The `pipeline` module composes, doesn't replace:

| Existing module | Role in pipeline |
|---|---|
| `hints` | `Pipeline::hint()` renders next-step hints at the workflow level |
| `error` | `Step::error` holds an `AxiError` for any failed step |
| `idempotency` | `StepStatus::Done` maps to `already_done()` signals per step — skip already-complete steps |
| `recovery` | `AxiError::recovery` on a failed step guides retry of that specific step |
| `toon` / `kv` | `Step::output` holds rendered TOON/KV from that step's API call |

---

## The expanded module list (12 modules)

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `toon` | TOON list rendering for N uniform-schema items |
| `kv` | Markdown-KV single-item/metadata rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` block construction |
| `truncate` | Char-boundary-safe truncation |
| `empty` | Definitive zero states |
| `error` | `AxiError`, `ErrorCode`, stdout errors, exit codes |
| `idempotency` | `already_done()`, `PartialSuccess`, `IdempotencyKey` |
| `resilience` | `RetryConfig`, `parse_retry_after()`, `next_retry_delay()` |
| `status` | `StatusResponse`, content-first orientation (P8) |
| `recovery` | `RecoveryHint`, recovery hint shapes |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — single-operation integration point |
| **`pipeline`** | **`Pipeline` builder — workflow-level integration point** |

`AgentResponse` remains the primary point for single operations. `Pipeline` is the primary point for multi-step workflows. They're siblings, not nested.

---

## The NAPI surface also grows

TypeScript MCP servers and CLIs need pipeline too:

```typescript
export declare class Pipeline {
  constructor(name: string);
  step(step: StepInput): this;
  parallel(steps: StepInput[]): this;
  hint(hint: string): this;
  render(): string;
  renderVerbose(): string;
  exitCode(): number;
}

export interface StepInput {
  name: string;
  status: 'pending' | 'running' | 'done' | 'skipped' | 'failed';
  summary?: string;
  output?: string;
  error?: string;  // serialized AxiError render
}
```

---

## One thing I want to validate before writing the design doc

The `progress:` line and `[parallel]` / `[sequential]` group headers are **new grammar productions** in TOON. That's a meaningful spec extension — agents trained on TOON without pipeline context won't know the group header syntax.

Two options:

**A) Extend the TOON grammar** — `[parallel]` / `[sequential]` become first-class productions. Clean, but every parser (including any test-only parsers) needs updating. Agents need to handle unknown header lines gracefully.

**B) Encode groups in the type name** — `pipeline_parallel[3]{...}:` and `pipeline_seq[3]{...}:` as separate TOON blocks within one response, separated by blank lines. Backward-compatible with the existing grammar — agents that don't know pipeline just see two TOON blocks.

I lean **B** — simpler for agents, no grammar extension, works today. The group structure is implicit in the block ordering rather than explicit headers.

Which do you prefer? Then I'll write the design doc covering both the original 11 modules and the new `pipeline` module.

content.text:
Strictly internal. The agent doesn't need to know *how* steps were executed — only what happened to each one.

From the agent's perspective, the grouping is irrelevant. It cares about:

- `post_review` failed
- `notify_team` was skipped
- What to do next

Whether `fetch_pr`, `fetch_checks`, and `fetch_diff` ran in parallel is the producer's implementation detail. The agent just sees three `done` rows.

So the rendered output stays flat TOON:

```
pipeline[5]{step,status,summary}:
  validate_input,done,"Schema OK"
  fetch_pr,done,"PR #42 — 3 files changed"
  fetch_checks,done,"3/3 passing"
  post_review,failed,"Unauthorized — check token scope"
  notify_team,skipped,""
progress: 3 done · 1 failed · 1 skipped
help[1]:
  Retry post_review after fixing token scope — prior steps already complete
```

The `Pipeline` builder exposes `parallel()` and `step()` as an API convenience so the consumer can express *intent* — which is useful for the builder to determine dependency ordering (e.g. auto-skip steps that depend on a failed parallel group). That logic is internal. It never surfaces in the string output.

The only new grammar production is the `progress:` summary line — which is small, unambiguous, and parseable by any agent that encounters it cold.

No grammar extension needed, no `[parallel]` markers. Clean.

---

Ready to write the design doc now. The full scope is:

- 12-module architecture (11 existing + `pipeline`)
- Workspace layout + tooling config (napi 3, divan, nextest, llvm-cov, deny, typos)
- CLAUDE.md content
- 8 agent session brief format (S0–S4, with parallel briefs per phase)
- CI workflow structure
- TOON grammar: only addition is `progress:` line for pipeline responses

content.text:
Now the full picture snaps into focus. This is **two crates**, not one.

---

## The layer separation

```
Monokl / Firkin / Lumen / Pulse
         │
         ▼
  [execution crate]          ← this spec: tokio, moka, nucleo, surface adapters
  PipelineExecutor, Cache,
  FuzzyResolver, Resilience
         │  uses for rendering
         ▼
      michi                  ← pure sync primitives, no runtime deps
  render_toon(), Pipeline,
  AxiError, hints, recovery
```

michi stays exactly as specced — pure computation, zero tokio, zero moka. The execution crate depends on michi for formatting its output. When `McpSink::into_response_body()` needs to produce agent-readable step status, it uses `michi::Pipeline::render()`. When a step fails and needs an agent-readable error, it reaches for `michi::AxiError`.

This is the same pattern michi already models internally: `resilience.rs` gives you `next_retry_delay()` (pure computation); the execution crate's `with_resilience()` does the actual async loop using that delay value. Two distinct responsibilities, clear ownership.

---

## What this means for michi's `pipeline` module

The `pipeline` module I proposed for michi IS still needed — it's the typed rendering interface the execution crate builds against. But its scope is now precisely defined:

**In michi (pure data + rendering):**
```rust
pub struct Pipeline { name, steps, hints }
pub struct Step { name, status, summary, output, error }
pub enum StepStatus { Pending, Running, Done, Skipped, Failed }
impl Pipeline { fn render(&self) -> String }   // → TOON string
```

**In the execution crate (execution + results):**
```rust
pub struct PipelineResult { run_id, status, completed, failed, checkpoint }
pub struct PipelineExecutor { /* tokio-backed */ }
```

The execution crate converts its `PipelineResult` → michi's `Pipeline` → rendered string. The conversion is a thin adapter, not a deep coupling.

---

## The `AgentError` / `AxiError` question

The execution crate defines `AgentError` (HTTP, Timeout, Cancelled, etc.) and michi defines `AxiError` (InvalidInput, NotFound, RateLimited, etc.). These are parallel, not competing — they model different things:

- `AgentError` = what went wrong during execution (infrastructure perspective)
- `AxiError` = what to tell the agent (response formatting perspective)

The execution crate maps `AgentError → AxiError` when it needs to produce agent-readable output. That mapping lives in the execution crate, not in michi. Concretely:

```rust
// In execution crate — converts execution failure to michi agent output
fn to_axi_error(e: &AgentError) -> michi::AxiError {
    match e {
        AgentError::Http { status: 429, retry_after, .. } =>
            michi::AxiError::new(michi::ErrorCode::RateLimited, e.to_string())
                .retry_after(retry_after.unwrap_or(Duration::from_secs(60))),
        AgentError::Timeout { .. } =>
            michi::AxiError::new(michi::ErrorCode::Timeout, e.to_string()),
        // ...
    }
}
```

Clean boundary. Neither crate knows about the other's internals.

---

## Crate naming

`agent-pipeline` is the placeholder. Given the orin-axi naming aesthetic (short, real word, earned metaphor):

**`kata`** — from 型 (Japanese: form, pattern, sequence of techniques). In martial arts, a kata is a choreographed sequence of movements practised as one unit. A pipeline is a kata: a named sequence of steps executed as a compound action. It also subtly echoes michi (道): michi is the path, kata is the form you practice on it.

Fits the suite table:

| Name | Origin | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| michi | Japanese (道) | path, way |
| **kata** | Japanese (型) | form, pattern, sequence |
| Monokl | Slavic/French | monocle |
| Firkin | Middle English | small barrel |
| Lumen | Latin | luminous flux |
| Pulse | Latin | vital sign |

---

## A few things to confirm before I write the design doc

**1. Same workspace or separate repos?**
The natural call is separate repos (`orin-axi/michi` and `orin-axi/kata`), since they have very different dependency profiles and release cadences. michi is stable primitives; kata will iterate faster. Agree?

**2. The spec's `ResiliencePolicy` vs michi's `ResilienceConfig`**
Both exist now. michi's is pure computation (no async). kata's wraps it in `with_resilience()` async. The field names differ slightly — should michi's be renamed to align, or is the naming divergence fine (different layers, different names)?

**3. Fuzzy matching scope for day one**
`nucleo-matcher` is a significant dependency. Is fuzzy a day-one requirement for kata v0.1, or is it the first thing to defer? The `FuzzyResolver` is cleanly isolated — it could ship as `todo!()` stubs behind a `fuzzy` feature flag with the trait boundary already in place.

**4. NAPI for kata?**
michi gets a NAPI wrapper (`michi-node`) because TypeScript MCP servers need its rendering primitives. Does kata need NAPI? Or is kata Rust-only, with TypeScript MCP servers consuming it indirectly through michi's npm package?

lastPrompt: Do we need a separate crate or should it all be one michi agentic crate/library?

content.text:
One crate. Here's the reasoning:

---

## Why one crate wins

**Feature flags give you the same guarantee as separate crates.** A consumer who just wants `render_toon()` adds `michi` with default features and pulls in zero tokio, zero moka, zero nucleo. The "pure computation" principle isn't enforced by convention — it's enforced by cargo:

```toml
[features]
default  = []                                           # pure sync, zero runtime
pipeline = ["dep:tokio", "dep:tokio-util",
            "dep:async-trait", "dep:uuid"]              # execution layer
fuzzy    = ["dep:nucleo-matcher", "pipeline"]           # fuzzy + pipeline
cache    = ["dep:moka", "pipeline"]                     # caching tier
cli      = ["dep:indicatif", "dep:inquire",
            "dep:crossterm", "dep:ctrlc", "pipeline"]   # CLI adapters
mcp      = ["pipeline"]                                 # MCP adapters (pure logic)
napi     = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]              # npm wrapper
full     = ["pipeline", "fuzzy", "cache", "cli", "mcp"]
```

A Rust CLI that runs pipelines: `michi = { features = ["cli"] }`. An MCP server: `michi = { features = ["mcp"] }`. A tool that just formats output: `michi` with no features.

**The suite tools always want both.** Monokl, Firkin, Lumen, Pulse all need rendering primitives AND pipeline execution. Two crates means two deps, two version pins, two changelogs to track, two sets of breaking changes to coordinate. With one crate they write:

```toml
michi = { version = "0.1", features = ["cli"] }
```

That's the entire dependency story.

**Unified types eliminate the translation layer.** With two crates you need `AgentError → AxiError` conversions at the boundary. With one crate, there's one error type. The pipeline executor and the rendering functions live in the same type system — `michi::Error` carries both execution context and rendering semantics.

**One crates.io entry, one npm package.** External consumers discover one thing, version one thing, trust one API surface.

---

## What the unified module structure looks like

```
src/
  lib.rs

  // ── Always compiled (default features) ──────────────────────────────────
  toon/             render_toon(), ToonOptions, Value, escape
  kv/               render_kv(), KvItem, KvValue
  hints.rs          Hint, render_hints(), append_hints()
  truncate.rs       truncate(), truncate_inline()
  empty.rs          empty_state()
  error.rs          Error (unified), ErrorClass, Sensitive<T>
  recovery.rs       RecoveryHint, render_recovery()
  status.rs         StatusResponse, Health (pure render, no async)
  response.rs       AgentResponse builder
  idempotency.rs    IdempotencyKey, already_done(), PartialSuccess

  resilience/
    mod.rs          RetryConfig, next_retry_delay(), parse_retry_after() ← always
    policy.rs       with_resilience()                                    ← pipeline feature
    circuit.rs      CircuitBreaker                                       ← pipeline feature

  pipeline/
    mod.rs          Pipeline, Step, StepStatus (pure data + render)      ← always
    executor.rs     PipelineExecutor, PipelineContext                    ← pipeline feature
    step.rs         StepFn, StepContext, SkipReason                     ← pipeline feature
    graph.rs        assign_levels(), cycle detection                     ← pipeline feature
    result.rs       PipelineResult, RunStatus                           ← pipeline feature
    checkpoint.rs   Checkpoint, CheckpointStore, NoopCheckpointStore    ← pipeline feature

  // ── Optional features ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  fuzzy/            FuzzyMatcher, FuzzyResolver, Disambiguator           ← fuzzy feature
  cache/            Cache, CachePolicy, DiskCache                        ← cache feature

  sink/             OutputSink, AgentEvent, NoopSink                     ← pipeline feature
  telemetry/        TelemetryProvider, NoopProvider                      ← always (zero-cost)

  adapters/
    cli/            HumanWriter, JsonWriter, DiskCheckpointStore,
                    TtyDisambiguator, install_ctrl_c_handler              ← cli feature
    mcp/            McpSink, McpDisambiguator, MemoryCheckpointStore     ← mcp feature

  napi.rs           #[napi] exports                                      ← napi feature
```

The pure/async split within modules follows the same pattern tokio uses internally — the sync computation is always compiled, the async extension is gated. For `resilience`, that means `next_retry_delay()` is always there; `with_resilience()` requires the `pipeline` feature.

---

## The error type consolidation

One crate means one error type. The current spec has `AxiError` (michi, rendering-focused) and `AgentError` (execution spec, infrastructure-focused). In a unified crate these merge:

```rust
// src/error.rs
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum Error {
    // Execution errors (pipeline feature)
    #[error("HTTP {status}: {message}")]
    Http { status: u16, message: String, retryable: bool, retry_after: Option<Duration> },
    #[error("Timeout after {elapsed:?}")]
    Timeout { elapsed: Duration },
    #[error("Cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    // ... other AgentError variants

    // Domain errors (always)
    #[error("{0}")]
    InvalidInput(String),
    #[error("Not found: {0}")]
    NotFound(String),
    // ...
}

impl Error {
    pub fn render(&self) -> String { ... }   // agent-readable stdout string
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32 { 1 }
    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool { ... }
    pub fn class(&self) -> ErrorClass { ... }
}
```

`Sensitive<T>` stays. `ErrorClass` stays. The rendering methods (`render()`, `exit_code()`) live on the unified type so any error anywhere in the library can be formatted for agent consumption without a conversion step.

---

## Only one thing stays separate

The NAPI wrapper (`packages/michi-node`) must be a separate Cargo crate — Rust requires `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` for native Node addons, which can't coexist with a regular `lib` in the same crate. But this is a build artifact detail, not a conceptual split. `michi-node` is a thin shim that re-exports from the unified `michi` crate and wraps it for Node.

---

The name `michi` holds. One crate, one identity, one version. Everything from rendering primitives to async pipeline execution lives under `michi::`. Ready to write the design doc?

```

The `packages/michi-node` crate has to exist as a separate Cargo crate because Node native addons require `crate-type = ["cdylib"]`, which can't coexist with a regular `[lib]` in the same `Cargo.toml`. That's the only reason for the split — it's a build artifact, not a conceptual boundary.

`michi-node` has essentially no logic. It's a thin shim:

```rust
// packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs
#[napi]
pub fn render_toon(opts: RenderToonOptions) -> String {
    michi::render_toon(/* convert opts */)
}
```

All substance lives in the root `michi` crate. Same pattern as oxc-react-codegen:

```
oxc-react-codegen/
  crates/core/        ← all the logic
  crates/binding/     ← thin NAPI cdylib shim
  crates/cli/         ← thin CLI binary
```

michi is the same shape, just smaller:

```
michi/
  src/               ← all the logic (one crate, feature-gated)
  packages/
    michi-node/      ← thin NAPI cdylib shim
```

That's it. One repo, one workspace, two members — for a build constraint, not an architectural one. Ready to write the design doc now?

content.text:
No. michi is too small to justify it.

Moon earns its place in large polyglot monorepos where you need affected-file task routing, cross-language dependency graphs, and aggressive caching across many projects. The value compounds with scale.

michi is two Cargo crates and a thin JS shim. The coordination problem Moon solves doesn't exist here:

- **Cargo** already handles the Rust workspace dependency graph
- **pnpm** (one `package.json` in `packages/michi-node`) handles the JS side
- **GitHub Actions** with `Swatinem/rust-cache` + pnpm's built-in cache handles CI speed

oxc-react-codegen has more JS complexity than michi (vite plugin, install matrix, multiple Node consumers) and doesn't use Moon.

Revisit if orin-axi ever consolidates Monokl, Firkin, Lumen, Pulse into a single monorepo — at that point Moon's affected detection and cross-project task graph would pay off. Not now.

Cargo + pnpm + Actions. That's the stack. Ready to write the design doc?

content.text:
Yes to both. Here's how similar NAPI repos handle it and what fits michi.

---

## How other Rust + NAPI repos do it

Most follow one of two patterns:

**Pattern A — napi-rs template (npm package at root):** The repo root IS the npm package. Works for pure binding crates with no separate library. Not our shape — michi has a real Rust lib.

**Pattern B — workspace with binding subpackage (what we want):** Rust workspace at root, NAPI cdylib in a subdirectory. This is what oxc-react-codegen does, what SWC does, what Rolldown does. The binding is a build artifact of the library, not a peer.

---

## just + pnpm: yes

`just` is the single local interface across both Rust and JS. Developers run one tool regardless of which layer they're touching. pnpm handles the JS package in `packages/michi-node`. CI uses raw commands explicitly — just is for local ergonomics.

```justfile
# justfile

# List available recipes
default:
    @just --list

# ── Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

build:
    cargo build --workspace

build-release:
    cargo build --release --workspace

# Build the NAPI npm package (debug)
build-node:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform

# Build NAPI release binaries for publish
build-node-release:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform --release

# ── Test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test: test-rust test-node

test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace

test-node: build-node
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm test

# ── Lint ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

check: fmt-check clippy deny typos

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

fmt-check:
    cargo fmt --all --check

clippy:
    cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings

deny:
    cargo deny check

typos:
    typos

# ── Snapshots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

snapshots:
    cargo insta review

# ── Benchmarks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

bench:
    cargo bench --workspace

# ── Coverage ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info

# ── Full pre-push check ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ci: check test bench
```

---

## pnpm workspace root — probably not

For v0.1 there's one JS package. A pnpm workspace root (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` + root `package.json`) adds ceremony for no gain right now. The justfile `cd`s into `packages/michi-node` for JS commands. Add the workspace root when a second JS package appears.

---

## Final repo shape

```
michi/
  Cargo.toml              ← [workspace] + [package] (michi lib)
  Cargo.lock
  rust-toolchain.toml     ← pinned stable toolchain
  build.rs                ← napi-build (feature-gated)
  justfile                ← task runner
  .rustfmt.toml
  .clippy.toml
  .typos.toml
  deny.toml
  CLAUDE.md
  README.md
  src/
    lib.rs
    toon/
    kv/
    hints.rs  truncate.rs  empty.rs  error.rs
    recovery.rs  status.rs  response.rs  idempotency.rs
    resilience/
    pipeline/
    fuzzy/       ← fuzzy feature
    cache/       ← cache feature
    sink/
    telemetry/
    adapters/
      cli/       ← cli feature
      mcp/       ← mcp feature
    napi.rs      ← napi feature
  benches/
    toon_render.rs
    kv_render.rs
  tests/
    toon_integration.rs
    kv_integration.rs
    resilience_integration.rs
    idempotency_integration.rs
    snapshot_tests.rs
  packages/
    michi-node/
      Cargo.toml           ← crate-type = ["cdylib"]
      package.json         ← name: "michi", published to npmjs
      index.js             ← platform loadBinding
      index.d.ts           ← generated by napi-derive
      src/lib.rs
      __test__/
        index.test.mjs
  .github/
    workflows/
      ci.yml
  docs/
    00-overview.md
    01-spec.md
    projects/
      01-mvp.md
      agents/              ← session briefs for S0–S4
```

---

That's the shape. One repo, one workspace, `just` as the local task runner, pnpm scoped to the node package. No Moon, no workspace root package.json yet.

Ready to write the design doc now?
